# Nepali Date Library

> Universal, production-ready multi-language ecosystem for working with Nepali (Bikram Sambat / BS) dates. Supports NodeJS/TypeScript, Python, and PHP with unified APIs, zero dependencies, and annually audited calendar data verified up to the active year.

## Official Resources
- Website: https://nepali-pkg.date
- Date Converter Suite: https://nepali-pkg.date/converter
- Nepali Calendar (Patro): https://nepali-pkg.date/calendar
- Full Documentation: https://nepali-pkg.date/docs
- Complete AI Reference: https://nepali-pkg.date/llms-full.txt
- GitHub Organization: https://github.com/SandipGhimire/Nepali-Date

## Package Ecosystem & Installation
- **NodeJS / TypeScript**: `npm install nepali-date-library` (npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/nepali-date-library, GitHub: https://github.com/SandipGhimire/Nepali-Date-Library-NodeJS)
- **Python**: `pip install nepali-date-library` (PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/nepali-date-library/, GitHub: https://github.com/SandipGhimire/Nepali-Date-Library-Python)
- **PHP**: `composer require sghimire/nepali-date-library` (Packagist: https://packagist.org/packages/sghimire/nepali-date-library, GitHub: https://github.com/SandipGhimire/Nepali-Date-Library-PHP)

## Core Capabilities
- **Bidirectional Date Conversion**: Convert Gregorian (AD) to Bikram Sambat (BS) and Bikram Sambat (BS) to Gregorian (AD).
- **Calendar Range & Annual Audits**: Spans 1976/01/01 BS to 2100/12/31 BS (approx 1919-04-13 to 2044-04-12 AD). Dates up to the active year are verified against official Government of Nepal gazettes. Every year in Ashwin (Ashoj), mapping tables are updated with official solar ingress corrections upon release of the new calendar.
- **Date Manipulation & Arithmetic**: Add or subtract days, months, and years with automatic edge-case handling for variable Nepali month lengths (29 to 32 days).
- **Government of Nepal Fiscal Year**: Native support for Nepali fiscal years (Shrawan 1 to Ashadh end), fiscal quarters (Q1: Shrawan-Ashwin, Q2: Kartik-Poush, Q3: Magh-Chaitra, Q4: Baisakh-Ashadh).
- **Formatting & Localization**: Flexible date format tokens (`YYYY-MM-DD`, `DD MMMM YYYY`, `dddd`, etc.) rendered in English and Devanagari numerals and script.
- **Date Comparison & Queries**: Check `isBefore`, `isAfter`, `isSame`, `isLeapYear`, `startOfMonth`, `endOfMonth`, `startOfYear`, `endOfYear`.

## Common Search Keywords & Queries
- **Date Converter**: Nepali date converter, Bikram Sambat date converter, BS to AD converter, AD to BS converter, English date to Nepali date, convert BS to AD, convert AD to BS.
- **Nepali Date & Calendar**: Nepali date, Nepali date library, Bikram Sambat, Bikram Sambat calendar, BS date, BS calendar, Nepali calendar online, Nepali patro, Nepali miti, today Nepali date, aajako Nepali date, aajako miti.
- **Calculators & Utilities**: Nepali age calculator, Nepali date difference calculator, Nepali date arithmetic, add days to Nepali date, Bikram Sambat leap year.
- **Fiscal Year (Aarthik Barsha)**: Nepal Government fiscal year calculator, Shrawan to Ashadh fiscal year, fiscal quarters (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4).
- **SDKs & Package Managers**: `nepali-date-library` on npm (Node.js/TypeScript), `nepali-date-library` on PyPI (Python), `sghimire/nepali-date-library` on Packagist (PHP).

## Quick Start Code Recipes

### NodeJS / TypeScript
```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// Current Nepali date
const today = new NepaliDate();
console.log(today.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // e.g. 2081-06-29

// Convert AD to BS
const bs = NepaliDate.fromAD(new Date("2024-10-15"));
console.log(bs.format("DD MMMM YYYY")); // 29 Ashwin 2081

// Date manipulation
bs.addDays(30);

// Nepal Fiscal Year
console.log(bs.getFiscalYear()); // 2081/82
```

### Python
```python
from nepali_date_library import NepaliDate
from datetime import date

# Current Nepali date
today = NepaliDate()
print(today.format("YYYY-MM-DD"))

# Convert AD to BS
bs = NepaliDate.from_ad(date(2024, 10, 15))
print(bs.format("DD MMMM YYYY"))

# Date manipulation
bs.add_days(30)

# Nepal Fiscal Year
print(bs.get_fiscal_year()) # 2081/82
```

### PHP
```php
use NepaliDateLibrary\NepaliDate;
use DateTime;

// Current Nepali date
$today = new NepaliDate();
echo $today->format("YYYY-MM-DD");

// Convert AD to BS
$bs = NepaliDate::fromAD(new DateTime("2024-10-15"));
echo $bs->format("DD MMMM YYYY");

// Date manipulation
$bs->addDays(30);

// Nepal Fiscal Year
echo $bs->getFiscalYear(); // 2081/82
```

- [NepaliDate.get_calendar_days() (PYTHON)](https://nepali-pkg.date/docs/python/static/get-calendar-days): [PYTHON] Static utility to generate a complete forty two cell calendar grid matrix for any month and year. Official API reference and code examples for Python.
- [NepaliDate.get_day_name() (PYTHON)](https://nepali-pkg.date/docs/python/static/get-day-name): [PYTHON] Static utility to retrieve the localized English or Nepali name for any day of the week index. Official API reference and code examples for Python.
- [NepaliDate.get_month_name() (PYTHON)](https://nepali-pkg.date/docs/python/static/get-month-name): [PYTHON] Static utility to retrieve the localized English or Nepali month name for any month index. Official API reference and code examples for Python.
- [NepaliDate.is_valid() (PYTHON)](https://nepali-pkg.date/docs/python/static/is-valid): [PYTHON] Static validation function to verify whether a given year, month, and day combination forms a valid Bikram Sambat date. Official API reference and code examples for Python.
- [NepaliDate.maximum() (PYTHON)](https://nepali-pkg.date/docs/python/static/maximum): [PYTHON] Static method returning the maximum supported date boundary for the NepaliDate calendar engine. Official API reference and code examples for Python.
- [NepaliDate.minimum() (PYTHON)](https://nepali-pkg.date/docs/python/static/minimum): [PYTHON] Static method returning the minimum supported date boundary for the NepaliDate calendar engine. Official API reference and code examples for Python.


---

# Detailed API Specifications & Reference Manual

## Bikram Sambat Calendar Structure
Bikram Sambat is a solar calendar historically used in Nepal and parts of South Asia. It is roughly 56.7 years ahead of the Gregorian (AD) calendar:
- Year range: 1976 BS to 2100 BS.
- Month names in order:
  1. Baisakh (बैशाख) - 30 to 31 days
  2. Jestha (जेठ) - 31 to 32 days
  3. Ashadh (असार) - 31 to 32 days
  4. Shrawan (साउन) - 31 to 32 days
  5. Bhadra (भदौ) - 31 to 32 days
  6. Ashwin (असोज) - 30 to 31 days
  7. Kartik (कार्तिक) - 29 to 30 days
  8. Mangsir (मंसिर) - 29 to 30 days
  9. Poush (पौष) - 29 to 30 days
  10. Magh (माघ) - 29 to 30 days
  11. Falgun (फागुन) - 29 to 30 days
  12. Chaitra (चैत) - 30 to 31 days

## Nepal Government Fiscal Year (आर्थिक वर्ष)
- Starts: Shrawan 1 (approx mid-July AD)
- Ends: Ashadh end (approx mid-July next year AD)
- Format: "YYYY/YY" (e.g., 2081/82)
- Fiscal Quarters:
  - First Quarter (Q1): Shrawan 1 to Ashwin end
  - Second Quarter (Q2): Kartik 1 to Poush end
  - Third Quarter (Q3): Magh 1 to Chaitra end
  - Fourth Quarter (Q4): Baisakh 1 to Ashadh end

## Formatting Tokens Cheat Sheet
- `YYYY`: 4-digit Nepali Year (e.g. 2081)
- `YY`: 2-digit Nepali Year (e.g. 81)
- `MMMM`: Full Nepali Month Name (e.g. Ashwin / असोज)
- `MMM`: Short Nepali Month Name (e.g. Ash / असो)
- `MM`: 2-digit Month (01-12)
- `M`: 1 or 2-digit Month (1-12)
- `DD`: 2-digit Day (01-32)
- `D`: 1 or 2-digit Day (1-32)
- `dddd`: Full Day Name (e.g. Sunday / आइतबार)
- `ddd`: Short Day Name (e.g. Sun / आइत)
- `HH`: 2-digit Hours (00-23)
- `mm`: 2-digit Minutes (00-59)
- `ss`: 2-digit Seconds (00-59)

## Page: Contribution Guide (/docs/contribution)
Description: Learn how to contribute to the Nepali Date Library ecosystem across Node.js, Python, PHP, and Documentation.

Thank you for your interest in contributing to the **Nepali Date (Bikram Sambat) Ecosystem**! This open-source project is built and maintained to provide synchronized, robust, zero-dependency calendar tools across JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, and PHP.

Whether you are fixing a typo, adding calendar tests, improving performance, or porting new features across languages, your contributions are warmly welcomed.

---

## Ecosystem Repositories

The ecosystem consists of four main projects:

| Project | Ecosystem | Source Repository |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Node.js / TypeScript** | npm, yarn, pnpm, bun | [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/SandipGhimire/Nepali-Date-Library-NodeJS) |
| **Python** | PyPI (uv, pip, poetry) | [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/SandipGhimire/Nepali-Date-Library-Python) |
| **PHP** | Packagist (Composer) | [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/SandipGhimire/Nepali-Date-Library-PHP) |
| **Documentation & Converter** | Next.js 16 / Fumadocs | [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/SandipGhimire/Nepali-Date-Library) |

---

## Core Contribution Principles

Before proposing changes, please keep our core architectural principles in mind:

1. **Zero External Runtime Dependencies**:
   All three language packages (`nepali-date-library`) MUST maintain zero external dependencies at runtime. Do not add runtime packages.

2. **Standardized Cross-Language Semantics**:
   The API surface across Node.js, Python, and PHP is intentionally synchronized. Method names, formatting tokens (e.g. `YYYY-MM-DD`, `dddd`), fiscal year quarters, and edge case handling should match across all implementations.

3. **Annual Calendar Verification & Range Coverage (1976 – 2100 BS)**:
   Dates up to the current active calendar year are verified against official Government of Nepal publications (Nepal Panchanga Nirnayak Samiti). Every year around the month of **Ashwin (Ashoj)**, when the official government calendar is released for the upcoming year, the mapping tables are audited and updated with exact solar ingress corrections. Test suites must pass across all supported years (1976/01/01 to 2100/12/31 BS).

4. **Deterministic Timezone Isolation**:
   Date arithmetic, weekday getters, and day start/end calculations must execute deterministically regardless of the host machine's local timezone.

## Page: Examples & Practical Recipes (/docs/examples)
Description: Real-world patterns and cross-language code recipes for working with Nepali dates.

Practical, copy-pasteable patterns for common tasks when working with Bikram Sambat dates across **Node.js / TypeScript**, **PHP**, and **Python**.

---

## 1. Storing User-Entered BS Date in Database

A recommended architecture pattern is to accept Bikram Sambat dates from user forms, convert them to standard Gregorian (AD) ISO dates for SQL/NoSQL storage, and convert back to BS when rendering.

### Node.js / TypeScript
```typescript
import { NepaliDate, BStoAD, ADtoBS } from "nepali-date-library";

// 1. User submits BS date: "2081-06-29"
const userBSInput = "2081-06-29";

// 2. Convert to AD for database insertion
const adDateString = BStoAD(userBSInput); // "2024-10-15"
// db.users.insert({ birth_date: new Date(adDateString) })

// 3. When reading from database, convert back to BS
const dbAdDate = "2024-10-15";
const displayBSDate = ADtoBS(dbAdDate); // "2081-06-29"
```

### PHP
```php
use NepaliDateLibrary\NepaliDate;
use function NepaliDateLibrary\BStoAD;
use function NepaliDateLibrary\ADtoBS;

$userBSInput = '2081-06-29';

// Convert to AD for database (MySQL DATE column)
$adDate = BStoAD($userBSInput); // '2024-10-15'

// Convert back to BS for presentation
$displayBS = ADtoBS($adDate); // '2081-06-29'
```

### Python
```python
from nepali_date_library import BStoAD, ADtoBS

user_bs = "2081-06-29"

# Convert to Gregorian for Django / SQLAlchemy model
ad_str = BStoAD(user_bs) # "2024-10-15"

# Convert back to BS
display_bs = ADtoBS(ad_str) # "2081-06-29"
```

---

## 2. Calculating Age from a Bikram Sambat Date of Birth

Calculate precise age breakdown (Years, Months, Days) from a BS date of birth:

### Node.js / TypeScript
```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

function calculateAge(dobBS: string) {
  const birth = new NepaliDate(dobBS);
  const today = new NepaliDate(); // Today in BS

  let years = today.getYear() - birth.getYear();
  let months = today.getMonth() - birth.getMonth();
  let days = today.getDate() - birth.getDate();

  if (days < 0) {
    months -= 1;
    days += 30; // approximate month adjustment
  }
  if (months < 0) {
    years -= 1;
    months += 12;
  }

  return { years, months, days };
}

console.log(calculateAge("2064-03-23"));
// { years: 17, months: 3, days: 6 }
```

---

## 3. Nepali Fiscal Year & Quarterly Reporting

The Nepali fiscal year runs from **1 Shrawan (Month 4)** to **Ashadh end (Month 3)**.

### PHP (Laravel / Accounting)
```php
use NepaliDateLibrary\NepaliDate;

$date = new NepaliDate('2081-06-29');

// Get Fiscal Year string
echo $date->getFiscalYear(); // "2081/82"

// Get Quarter (1 to 4)
echo $date->getQuarter(); // 1 (Shrawan - Ashoj)

// Get Start and End dates of Q2 (Kartik to Poush)
$q2 = NepaliDate::getQuarter(2, 2081);
echo "Q2 Start: " . $q2['start']->format('YYYY-MM-DD'); // 2081-07-01
echo "Q2 End: " . $q2['end']->format('YYYY-MM-DD');     // 2081-09-29
```

### Node.js / TypeScript
```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date = new NepaliDate("2081-06-29");
console.log(`Fiscal Year: ${date.getFiscalYear()}`); // "2081/82"
console.log(`Fiscal Quarter: Q${date.getQuarter()}`); // "Q1"
```

---

## 4. Date Arithmetic & Expiry Tracking

Add or subtract days, months, and years with built-in month-length clamping:

### Python
```python
from nepali_date_library import NepaliDate

subscription = NepaliDate("2081-01-31")

# Add 1 month (safely clamps to Jestha end without month overflow)
subscription.add_months(1)
print("Next renewal:", subscription.format("YYYY-MM-DD"))

# Add 15 days
subscription.add_days(15)
print("Grace period:", subscription.format("YYYY-MM-DD"))
```

### Node.js / TypeScript
```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const contract = new NepaliDate("2081-01-15");

// 90-day review period
contract.addDays(90);
console.log(contract.format("DDDD, MMMM D, YYYY"));
```

---

## 5. Devanagari Localization & Formatting

Render authentic Nepali dates with native script and Devanagari numerals:

### Node.js / TypeScript
```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date = new NepaliDate("2081-07-15");

// English formatting
console.log(date.format("YYYY MMMM DD, DDDD"));
// "2081 Kartik 15, Friday"

// Devanagari Nepali script formatting
console.log(date.format("yyyy mmmm dd, dddd"));
// "२०८१ कार्तिक १५, शुक्रबार"
```

## Quick Start

```typescript
import { NepaliDate, ADtoBS, BStoAD } from "nepali-date-library";

// 1. Current Nepali date
const today = new NepaliDate();
console.log(today.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // e.g. "2081-06-29"

// 2. Parse a BS date
const event = new NepaliDate("2081-07-15");
console.log(event.format("DDDD, MMMM D, YYYY")); // "Friday, Kartik 15, 2081"

// 3. Convert to JavaScript Date (Gregorian AD)
const adDate = event.toJsDate();
console.log(adDate.toISOString()); // "2024-10-31T18:15:00.000Z"

// 4. Standalone conversion helpers
const bs = ADtoBS("2024-11-15"); // "2081-07-30"
const ad = BStoAD("2081-07-30"); // "2024-11-15"
```

---

## Core Capabilities

- **Strict TypeScript Types**: Fully typed with comprehensive IntelliSense and autocomplete.
- **Zero Runtime Dependencies**: Ultra-lightweight footprint suitable for Node.js, React, Next.js, and edge workers.
- **Bidirectional Conversion**: Accurate conversion between Gregorian (AD) and Bikram Sambat (BS) from 1976 to 2100 BS.
- **Date Arithmetic**: Add and subtract days, months, and years with accurate month-day boundary clamping.
- **Fiscal Year Engine**: Built-in calculation for Nepali fiscal years (Shrawan to Ashadh) and financial quarters.
- **Devanagari Localization**: Native formatting with Nepali numerals (`२०८१`), month names (`कार्तिक`), and weekdays (`शुक्रबार`).

## Page: new NepaliDate() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/class/constructor)
Description: [NodeJS] Constructor overloads and initialization options for creating NepaliDate instances in Node.js and TypeScript. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `NepaliDate` constructor creates instances representing specific points in time mapped to the Bikram Sambat calendar system. You can construct an instance representing the current moment, provide separate year, month, and day integers, supply a standard date string, or pass a native JavaScript Date object. Bikram Sambat months are indexed starting from 0 for Baisakh through 11 for Chaitra.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

```javascript
const { NepaliDate } = require("nepali-date-library");
```

---

## Signatures

```typescript
// 1. Current Date & Time
new NepaliDate(): NepaliDate;

// 2. From Gregorian Date Object
new NepaliDate(date: Date): NepaliDate;

// 3. From Formatted Date String
new NepaliDate(dateString: string): NepaliDate;

// 4. From Coordinates (Year, Month, Day)
new NepaliDate(year: number, month: number, day: number): NepaliDate;

// 5. From Unix Epoch Milliseconds
new NepaliDate(timestamp: number): NepaliDate;

// 6. From Existing Instance (Cloning)
new NepaliDate(date: NepaliDate): NepaliDate;
```

---

## Overload Details & Parameters

### 1. No Arguments
Constructs an instance set to the current system date and time.
```typescript
const now = new NepaliDate();
```

### 2. From JavaScript Date (`Date`)
Converts a native JavaScript `Date` to its corresponding Bikram Sambat date.
```typescript
const jsDate = new Date();
const date = new NepaliDate(jsDate);
```

### 3. From String (`string`)
Parses a date string formatted as `YYYY-MM-DD`, `YYYY/MM/DD`, or `YYYY.MM.DD`.
```typescript
const date1 = new NepaliDate("2081-07-15");
const date2 = new NepaliDate("2081/07/15");
const date3 = new NepaliDate("2081.07.15");
```

### 4. From Coordinates (`year, month, day`)
* `year`: 4-digit Bikram Sambat year (e.g. `2081`).
* `month`: **0-indexed** month (`0` for Baisakh to `11` for Chaitra).
* `day`: Day of month (`1` to `32`).
```typescript
// 2081 Kartik 15 (Month 6 is Kartik)
const date = new NepaliDate(2081, 6, 15);
```

### 5. From Timestamp (`number`)
Initializes the date from an epoch millisecond integer.
```typescript
const date = new NepaliDate(1730332800000);
```

---

## Exceptions

| Error Message | Trigger Condition |
| :--- | :--- |
| `Invalid argument syntax` | Thrown if parameters fail type checks or incomplete arguments are passed. |
| `Invalid date` | Thrown if string parsing encounters non-numeric components. |
| `Nepal year out of range` | Thrown if year is earlier than `1976` BS or later than `2100` BS. |
| `Invalid nepali month must be between 1 - 12` | Thrown if string month component is outside `1`–`12`. |
| `Invalid nepali date must be between 1 - <max> in <year> <month>` | Thrown if the day exceeds the days count for that specific month and year. |

---

## Examples

### Complete Constructor Variations

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// Current instant
const current = new NepaliDate();

// String parsing
const parsed = new NepaliDate("2080-01-01");

// Numeric coordinates (Month 0 = Baisakh)
const newYear = new NepaliDate(2082, 0, 1);

// From Gregorian Date
const fromAd = new NepaliDate(new Date("2024-10-31"));

// Copy constructor
const copy = new NepaliDate(parsed);
```

---

## Related

* [`NepaliDate.isValid()`](/docs/nodejs/static/is-valid): Validate coordinates prior to instantiation.
* [`date.clone()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/clone): Clone an instance via method call.
* [`date.parse()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/parse): Mutate an existing instance from a string.

## Page: Instance Properties (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/class/properties)
Description: [NodeJS] Reference for public instance properties available on every NepaliDate object including year, month, day, and underlying timestamp. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

Every `NepaliDate` instance provides direct read access to its core calendar coordinates through public properties. These include the four digit Bikram Sambat year, the month number indexed from 0 to 11, the day of the month from 1 to 32, and the underlying UTC timestamp stored as a native JavaScript Date object. These properties reflect the current state of the date instance after any modifications or arithmetic operations.

---

## Property Reference

| Property | Type | Description | Range |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `year` | `number` | The Bikram Sambat year. | `1976` – `2100` |
| `month` | `number` | The **0-indexed** Bikram Sambat month. | `0` (Baisakh) – `11` (Chaitra) |
| `day` | `number` | The day of the month. | `1` – `32` |
| `timestamp` | `Date` | The corresponding native JavaScript `Date` object in UTC. | Equivalent Gregorian timestamp |

---

## Examples

### Reading Properties Directly

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date = new NepaliDate("2081-07-15");

console.log(date.year);      // 2081
console.log(date.month);     // 6 (0-indexed: 6 corresponds to Kartik)
console.log(date.day);       // 15
console.log(date.timestamp); // 2024-10-31T00:00:00.000Z
```

### Direct Property vs. Method Access

While properties are public for inspection, it is recommended to use dedicated methods for formatting and mutation:

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date = new NepaliDate("2081-07-15");

// Using methods for formatted values
console.log(date.getDate()); // 15
console.log(date.getMonth() + 1); // 7 (1-indexed display)

// Using methods to mutate coordinates safely
date.setDate(16); // Safely validates days in month and recalculates timestamp
```

---

## Related

* [`new NepaliDate()`](/docs/nodejs/class/constructor): Instantiating a `NepaliDate` object.
* [`date.getEnglishDate()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/get-english-date): Retrieve the native JavaScript `Date`.

## Page: MONTH_EN (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/constants/month-en)
Description: [NodeJS] Array containing standard romanized English names of all twelve Bikram Sambat calendar months. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `MONTH_EN` constant is an immutable array containing the official romanized English names of the twelve Bikram Sambat months. The array is indexed starting from 0 for Baisakh up to index 11 for Chaitra, making it convenient for looking up month names corresponding to numeric month values returned by date methods.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { MONTH_EN } from "nepali-date-library";
```

## Value

```typescript
export const MONTH_EN = [
  "Baisakh",
  "Jestha",
  "Asar",
  "Shrawan",
  "Bhadra",
  "Aswin",
  "Kartik",
  "Mangsir",
  "Poush",
  "Magh",
  "Falgun",
  "Chaitra",
];
```

---

## Index Mapping

| Index | Month Name | Gregorian Equivalent (Approximate) |
| :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `0` | `"Baisakh"` | Mid-April to Mid-May |
| `1` | `"Jestha"` | Mid-May to Mid-June |
| `2` | `"Asar"` | Mid-June to Mid-July |
| `3` | `"Shrawan"` | Mid-July to Mid-August |
| `4` | `"Bhadra"` | Mid-August to Mid-September |
| `5` | `"Aswin"` | Mid-September to Mid-October |
| `6` | `"Kartik"` | Mid-October to Mid-November |
| `7` | `"Mangsir"` | Mid-November to Mid-December |
| `8` | `"Poush"` | Mid-December to Mid-January |
| `9` | `"Magh"` | Mid-January to Mid-February |
| `10` | `"Falgun"` | Mid-February to Mid-March |
| `11` | `"Chaitra"` | Mid-March to Mid-April |

---

## Examples

### Accessing Month Names by Index

```typescript
import { MONTH_EN, NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date = new NepaliDate("2081-01-15");
console.log(MONTH_EN[date.getMonth()]); // "Baisakh"
```

## Page: NEPALI_DATE_MAP (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/constants/nepali-date-map)
Description: [NodeJS] Historical calendar mapping table storing verified day counts for every Bikram Sambat month between 1976 and 2100 BS. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `NEPALI_DATE_MAP` data structure contains the calendar matrix for the Bikram Sambat system spanning years 1976 through 2100 BS. Because Bikram Sambat months have variable day counts determined by astronomical solar calculations rather than fixed rules, this mapping table provides the definitive source of truth for conversions, day calculations, and month lengths.

> [!NOTE]
> Dates up to the active calendar year are verified against official publications from the **Nepal Panchanga Nirnayak Samiti** (नेपाल पञ्चाङ्ग निर्णायक समिति). Every year around the month of **Ashwin (Ashoj)**, when the official government calendar is gazetted for the subsequent year, this mapping table is audited and updated with exact solar ingress corrections.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NEPALI_DATE_MAP } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Type Definition

```typescript
export const NEPALI_DATE_MAP: {
  year: number;
  days: number[];
  totalDays: number;
  daysTillNow: number;
}[];
```

---

## Object Schema

Each entry in the array represents one Bikram Sambat year and adheres to the following structure:

| Field | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `year` | `number` | The Bikram Sambat year (e.g. `2081`). |
| `days` | `number[]` | An array of 12 integers representing the day count of each month from Baisakh (`index 0`) to Chaitra (`index 11`). |
| `totalDays` | `number` | Total number of days in that Bikram Sambat year (typically `365` or `366`). |
| `daysTillNow` | `number` | Cumulative count of days elapsed from calendar epoch up to the end of this year. |

---

## Range and Epoch

* **Start Year**: `1976` BS (Gregorian equivalent: April 13, 1919)
* **End Year**: `2100` BS
* **Total Entries**: 125 historical and future astronomical calendar tables.

---

## Examples

### Accessing Year Metadata

```typescript
import { NEPALI_DATE_MAP } from "nepali-date-library";

// Find data for year 2081 BS
const year2081 = NEPALI_DATE_MAP.find((item) => item.year === 2081);

console.log(year2081?.year);       // 2081
console.log(year2081?.days);       // [31, 32, 31, 32, 31, 30, 30, 30, 29, 29, 30, 30]
console.log(year2081?.totalDays);  // 365
```

### Inspecting Specific Month Length

```typescript
import { NEPALI_DATE_MAP } from "nepali-date-library";

// 2081 Baisakh (index 0) has 31 days
const baisakhDays = NEPALI_DATE_MAP[2081 - 1976].days[0];
console.log(`2081 Baisakh has ${baisakhDays} days.`);
```

---

* [`NepaliDate.maximum()`](/docs/nodejs/static/maximum): Upper calendar limit.
* [`date.daysInMonth()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/days-in-month): Query days in a month.

## Page: NUMBER_NP (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/constants/number-np)
Description: [NodeJS] Array containing Devanagari numeral glyphs for digits zero through nine used for Nepali number localization. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `NUMBER_NP` constant is an array containing the ten Devanagari numeral characters representing digits 0 through 9 in Nepali script. It provides a direct lookup table for formatting numbers, years, dates, and currency values into native Devanagari script for Nepali language interfaces.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NUMBER_NP } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Value

```typescript
export const NUMBER_NP = ["०", "१", "२", "३", "४", "५", "६", "७", "८", "९"];
```

---

## Index Mapping

| Index | Character | Unicode Codepoint |
| :---: | :---: | :--- |
| `0` | `"०"` | `U+0966` |
| `1` | `"१"` | `U+0967` |
| `2` | `"२"` | `U+0968` |
| `3` | `"३"` | `U+0969` |
| `4` | `"४"` | `U+096A` |
| `5` | `"५"` | `U+096B` |
| `6` | `"६"` | `U+096C` |
| `7` | `"७"` | `U+096D` |
| `8` | `"८"` | `U+096E` |
| `9` | `"९"` | `U+096F` |

---

## Examples

### Converting Arabic Digits to Devanagari

```typescript
import { NUMBER_NP } from "nepali-date-library";

function toNepaliDigits(num: number | string): string {
  return String(num)
    .split("")
    .map((ch) => {
      const code = ch.charCodeAt(0) - 48;
      return code >= 0 && code <= 9 ? NUMBER_NP[code] : ch;
    })
    .join("");
}

console.log(toNepaliDigits(2081)); // "२०८१"
console.log(toNepaliDigits("2081-01-25")); // "२०८१-०१-२५"
```

* [`date.format()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/format): Format dates with lowercase tokens (`yyyy`, `mm`, `dd`).

* [`WEEK_SHORT_EN`](/docs/nodejs/constants/week-short-en): Abbreviated English weekday names.
* [`date.format()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/format): Formatting with the `ddd` token.

## Page: Date Converter Guide (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/date-converter)
Description: [NodeJS] Comprehensive guide to converting dates between Gregorian and Bikram Sambat calendar systems using standalone helper functions. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The date converter utilities provide pure standalone functions for converting date strings directly between the Gregorian calendar and the Bikram Sambat calendar. These functions operate without creating full class instances, making them suitable for high throughput batch processing, database migrations, and backend service integration.

---

## When to Use Helper Functions vs. the `NepaliDate` Class

| Requirement | Use `ADtoBS` / `BStoAD` | Use `NepaliDate` Class |
| :--- | :---: | :---: |
| Simple string-to-string conversion | Yes | Optional |
| Database serialization / ETL pipelines | Yes | Optional |
| Date arithmetic (`addDays`, `diff`) | No | Yes |
| Custom token formatting (`MMMM`, `dddd`) | No | Yes |
| Calendar boundary calculations (`startOfMonth`) | No | Yes |
| Fiscal year & quarter calculations | No | Yes |

---

## Timezone Drift Prevention

One of the most frequent bugs when converting dates in distributed environments is **single-day shifting caused by local server timezones**.

For example, parsing `"2024-11-01"` using `new Date("2024-11-01")` in a system running in UTC-5 (Eastern Time) produces `2024-10-31 19:00:00`, which erroneously converts to the previous Nepali date.

`ADtoBS` and `BStoAD` internally enforce **strict UTC parsing** via `Date.UTC`:
- `"2024-11-01"` is always resolved at `2024-11-01T00:00:00.000Z`.
- Conversions produce identical results regardless of whether your code runs in Tokyo (UTC+9), Kathmandu (UTC+5:45), London (UTC+0), or San Francisco (UTC-8).

---

## Input Format Standard

Both conversion functions enforce the ISO-8601 standard date format:

```text
YYYY-MM-DD
```

- Years must be 4 digits.
- Months must be 2 zero-padded digits (`01` to `12`).
- Days must be 2 zero-padded digits (`01` to `32`).

Passing strings with non-standard delimiters or single digits (e.g. `2081-7-5` or `2081/07/05`) will throw an explicit format error.

---

## Error Handling & `DateConversionError`

All conversion errors throw a descriptive exception or an instance of `DateConversionError` containing the underlying cause:

```typescript
import { ADtoBS } from "nepali-date-library";

try {
  const bsDate = ADtoBS("invalid-date-string");
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof Error) {
    console.error(error.message); // "Invalid date format. Expected format: YYYY-MM-DD"
  }
}
```

---

## Next Steps

Explore the individual function references:
- [`ADtoBS()`](/docs/nodejs/date-converter/ad-to-bs): Convert Gregorian AD strings to Bikram Sambat BS.
- [`BStoAD()`](/docs/nodejs/date-converter/bs-to-ad): Convert Bikram Sambat BS strings to Gregorian AD.

---

## Page: ADtoBS() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/date-converter/ad-to-bs)
Description: [NodeJS] Pure helper function to convert Gregorian calendar date strings into Bikram Sambat date strings. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `ADtoBS` function performs direct mathematical conversion of a Gregorian date string into its corresponding Bikram Sambat date string. It accepts standard date formats and returns the converted Nepali date, handling month day variations and leap year calculations automatically without external dependencies.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { ADtoBS } from "nepali-date-library";
```

```javascript
const { ADtoBS } = require("nepali-date-library");
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
function ADtoBS(adDate: string): string;
```

---

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- |
| `adDate` | `string` | Yes | Gregorian date string formatted strictly as `YYYY-MM-DD`. |

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `string`
* **Format**: `YYYY-MM-DD` representing the corresponding Bikram Sambat date.

---

## Exceptions

| Error Message | Trigger Condition |
| :--- | :--- |
| `Invalid date format. Expected format: YYYY-MM-DD` | Thrown if `adDate` fails the format regex `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$`. |
| `Invalid date input '<adDate>'` | Thrown if date values produce `NaN` (e.g. `2024-02-31`). |
| `DateConversionError: Failed to convert AD to BS` | Thrown if the date falls outside the verified ephemeris boundary (1919-04-13 to 2044-04-12 AD). |

---

## Examples

### Basic Conversion

```typescript
import { ADtoBS } from "nepali-date-library";

const bsDate = ADtoBS("2024-10-31");
console.log(bsDate); // "2081-07-15"
```

### Batch Array Processing

```typescript
import { ADtoBS } from "nepali-date-library";

const records = [
  { id: 1, createdAt: "2024-01-01" },
  { id: 2, createdAt: "2024-04-13" },
  { id: 3, createdAt: "2024-10-31" },
];

const mappedRecords = records.map((record) => ({
  ...record,
  createdAtBS: ADtoBS(record.createdAt),
}));

console.log(mappedRecords[0].createdAtBS); // "2080-09-16"
```

### Error Handling

```typescript
import { ADtoBS } from "nepali-date-library";

function safeADtoBS(dateString: string): string | null {
  try {
    return ADtoBS(dateString);
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

console.log(safeADtoBS("2024-10-31")); // "2081-07-15"
console.log(safeADtoBS("invalid")); // null
```

* [`new NepaliDate(date)`](/docs/nodejs/class/constructor): Converting a JavaScript Date object into a full `NepaliDate` instance.

## Page: BStoAD() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/date-converter/bs-to-ad)
Description: [NodeJS] Pure helper function to convert Bikram Sambat date strings into Gregorian calendar date strings. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `BStoAD` function converts a Bikram Sambat date string into its equivalent Gregorian calendar date string. It validates the input Nepali date against verified historical calendar maps and returns a formatted Gregorian date string suitable for storage in standard SQL databases or transmission over web APIs.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { BStoAD } from "nepali-date-library";
```

```javascript
const { BStoAD } = require("nepali-date-library");
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
function BStoAD(bsDate: string): string;
```

---

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- |
| `bsDate` | `string` | Yes | Bikram Sambat date string formatted strictly as `YYYY-MM-DD`. |

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `string`
* **Format**: `YYYY-MM-DD` representing the corresponding Gregorian date in UTC.

---

## Exceptions

| Error Message | Trigger Condition |
| :--- | :--- |
| `Invalid date format. Expected format: YYYY-MM-DD` | Thrown if `bsDate` fails the format regex `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$`. |
| `Nepal year out of range` | Thrown if year is earlier than `1976` BS or later than `2100` BS. |
| `Invalid nepali month must be between 1 - 12` | Thrown if month component is not within `1` to `12`. |
| `Invalid nepali date must be between 1 - <max> in <year> <month>` | Thrown if the day exceeds the verified days for that specific month and year. |
| `DateConversionError: Failed to convert BS to AD` | Wrapped error for conversion failures. |

---

## Examples

### Basic Conversion

```typescript
import { BStoAD } from "nepali-date-library";

const adDate = BStoAD("2081-07-15");
console.log(adDate); // "2024-10-31"
```

### Converting Month with 32 Days

Bikram Sambat summer months can contain 32 days. `BStoAD` validates the exact ephemeris for that year:

```typescript
import { BStoAD } from "nepali-date-library";

// Jestha 32, 2081
const adDate = BStoAD("2081-02-32");
console.log(adDate); // "2024-06-14"
```

### Database Persistence Pattern

Convert user-entered Bikram Sambat dates to standard ISO-8601 strings prior to storing in SQL or NoSQL databases:

```typescript
import { BStoAD } from "nepali-date-library";

interface UserRegistrationInput {
  fullName: string;
  birthDateBS: string; // e.g. "2055-04-12"
}

function prepareUserForStorage(input: UserRegistrationInput) {
  return {
    fullName: input.fullName,
    birthDateBS: input.birthDateBS,
    birthDateAD: BStoAD(input.birthDateBS), // "1998-07-27"
  };
}
```

## Page: Fiscal Year & Quarters Guide (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/fiscal-year)
Description: [NodeJS] Architecture and calculation rules for Nepal official fiscal year and quarterly trimester accounting cycles. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

In Nepal the official fiscal year begins on 1 Shrawan and ends on the final day of Ashadh in the following calendar year. The nepali date library includes specialized functions to compute fiscal years, identify trimester quarters, and determine quarter start and end boundary dates for financial, tax, and accounting systems.

---

## Fiscal Year Structure

Because the fiscal year starts in the fourth month of Bikram Sambat (Shrawan), every fiscal cycle spans two calendar years:

* **Format**: Standardized as `YYYY/YY` (e.g. `2081/82 BS`).
* **Start Date**: `1 Shrawan` (Month index `3`, Day `1`).
* **End Date**: `Last day of Ashadh` (Month index `2`, Day `31` or `32` of the succeeding calendar year).

---

## Fiscal Quarters (Trimesters)

The financial year is divided into four 3-month quarters:

| Quarter | Span (Bikram Sambat Months) | Typical Gregorian Span | Accounting Significance |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Q1** | 1 Shrawan – Last day of Ashwin | Mid-July to Mid-October | First trimester; Dashain festival preparations |
| **Q2** | 1 Kartik – Last day of Poush | Mid-October to Mid-January | Second trimester; mid-term budget review |
| **Q3** | 1 Magh – Last day of Chaitra | Mid-January to Mid-April | Third trimester; third-quarter corporate advance tax |
| **Q4** | 1 Baisakh – Last day of Ashadh | Mid-April to Mid-July | Final trimester; annual financial closing & tax filing |

> [!NOTE]
> Notice that **Q4** takes place in the succeeding Bikram Sambat calendar year (Baisakh, Jestha, Ashadh). The library automatically increments the calendar year when calculating Q4 boundaries.

---

## Fiscal Quarters vs. Calendar Quarters

`nepali-date-library` provides separate APIs for both systems:

* **Fiscal Quarters**: Used for taxation, corporate accounting, and financial reporting. Runs **Shrawan to Ashadh**.
* **Calendar Quarters**: Used for calendar quarters, seasonal reporting, and academic trimesters. Runs **Baisakh to Chaitra**.

---

## Section API Methods

Explore each dedicated function reference:
* [`NepaliDate.getCurrentFiscalYear()`](/docs/nodejs/fiscal-year/get-current-fiscal-year): Returns active fiscal year integer.
* [`date.getCurrentFiscalYearQuarter()`](/docs/nodejs/fiscal-year/get-current-fiscal-year-quarter): Returns quarter number (`1 | 2 | 3 | 4`) for a date.
* [`date.getCurrentFiscalYearQuarterDates()`](/docs/nodejs/fiscal-year/get-current-fiscal-year-quarter-dates): Returns `{ start, end }` dates for current quarter.
* [`NepaliDate.getFiscalYearQuarter()`](/docs/nodejs/fiscal-year/get-fiscal-year-quarter): Calculates boundaries for any arbitrary quarter and year.
* [`NepaliDate.getFiscalYearQuarters()`](/docs/nodejs/fiscal-year/get-fiscal-year-quarters): Returns all four fiscal quarters in a single call.
* [`Calendar Quarters`](/docs/nodejs/fiscal-year/calendar-quarters): Standard calendar quarters (`getQuarter` & `getQuarters`).

---

## Page: Calendar Quarters (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/fiscal-year/calendar-quarters)
Description: [NodeJS] Explanation of standard Bikram Sambat calendar quarters compared to government fiscal trimesters. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

Standard calendar quarters divide the Bikram Sambat calendar year into four equal three month periods starting from 1 Baisakh. This guide clarifies the structural difference between standard calendar quarters and Nepal government fiscal year trimesters, which commence three months later on 1 Shrawan.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

```javascript
const { NepaliDate } = require("nepali-date-library");
```

---

## Signatures

```typescript
static getQuarter(
  quarter: number,
  year?: number
): { start: NepaliDate; end: NepaliDate };

static getQuarters(
  year?: number
): {
  Q1: { start: NepaliDate; end: NepaliDate };
  Q2: { start: NepaliDate; end: NepaliDate };
  Q3: { start: NepaliDate; end: NepaliDate };
  Q4: { start: NepaliDate; end: NepaliDate };
};
```

---

## Calendar Quarter Alignment

| Quarter | Months (Bikram Sambat) | Span |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Q1** | Baisakh, Jestha, Ashadh | 1 Baisakh – Last day of Ashadh |
| **Q2** | Shrawan, Bhadra, Ashwin | 1 Shrawan – Last day of Ashwin |
| **Q3** | Kartik, Mangsir, Poush | 1 Kartik – Last day of Poush |
| **Q4** | Magh, Falgun, Chaitra | 1 Magh – Last day of Chaitra |

---

## Examples

### Getting a Single Calendar Quarter

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// Q1 of calendar year 2081 (Baisakh to Ashadh)
const q1 = NepaliDate.getQuarter(1, 2081);
console.log(q1.start.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2081-01-01"
console.log(q1.end.format("YYYY-MM-DD"));   // "2081-03-31"
```

### Getting All Four Calendar Quarters

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// Default year is current year
const quarters = NepaliDate.getQuarters(2081);

console.log("Q1:", quarters.Q1.start.format("YYYY-MM-DD"), "to", quarters.Q1.end.format("YYYY-MM-DD"));
console.log("Q2:", quarters.Q2.start.format("YYYY-MM-DD"), "to", quarters.Q2.end.format("YYYY-MM-DD"));
console.log("Q3:", quarters.Q3.start.format("YYYY-MM-DD"), "to", quarters.Q3.end.format("YYYY-MM-DD"));
console.log("Q4:", quarters.Q4.start.format("YYYY-MM-DD"), "to", quarters.Q4.end.format("YYYY-MM-DD"));
```

## Page: NepaliDate.getCurrentFiscalYear() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/fiscal-year/get-current-fiscal-year)
Description: [NodeJS] Method to retrieve the formatted fiscal year string for a given NepaliDate instance. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `getCurrentFiscalYear` method determines which official Nepalese fiscal year contains the current date instance. It returns a standardized fiscal year string such as 2081/82 based on whether the date falls before or after the 1 Shrawan fiscal transition boundary.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

```javascript
const { NepaliDate } = require("nepali-date-library");
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
static getCurrentFiscalYear(): number;
```

---

## Parameters

* None.

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `number`
* **Description**: The 4-digit Bikram Sambat year representing the beginning of the active fiscal cycle.

---

## Behavioral Logic

The method determines the current date and evaluates the month:
* If current month is **Baisakh, Jestha, or Ashadh** (months 0, 1, or 2), the fiscal cycle began in the previous calendar year. Returns `currentYear - 1`.
* If current month is **Shrawan through Chaitra** (months 3 through 11), the fiscal cycle began in the current calendar year. Returns `currentYear`.

---

## Examples

### Getting Current Fiscal Year Integer

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// If today is 2081 Kartik 15:
const fy = NepaliDate.getCurrentFiscalYear();
console.log(fy); // 2081
```

### Generating Formatted Fiscal Strings

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

function getFormattedFiscalYear(): string {
  const fy = NepaliDate.getCurrentFiscalYear();
  const nextShort = String(fy + 1).slice(-2);
  return `${fy}/${nextShort}`; // e.g. "2081/82"
}

console.log(getFormattedFiscalYear()); // "2081/82"
```

### Invoice Number Prefixing

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

function generateInvoiceNumber(sequence: number): string {
  const fy = NepaliDate.getCurrentFiscalYear();
  const fyTag = `${String(fy).slice(-2)}${String(fy + 1).slice(-2)}`; // "8182"
  const paddedSeq = String(sequence).padStart(5, "0");
  return `INV-${fyTag}-${paddedSeq}`;
}

console.log(generateInvoiceNumber(42)); // "INV-8182-00042"
```

* [`date.getCurrentFiscalYearQuarter()`](/docs/nodejs/fiscal-year/get-current-fiscal-year-quarter): Get the quarter number for a specific date.

## Page: date.getCurrentFiscalYearQuarter() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/fiscal-year/get-current-fiscal-year-quarter)
Description: [NodeJS] Method to calculate the active fiscal trimester quarter number for a NepaliDate instance. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `getCurrentFiscalYearQuarter` method returns an integer from 1 to 4 representing the active fiscal trimester of the current date. Because Nepal fiscal calendar starts in Shrawan, quarter 1 covers Shrawan through Ashwin, quarter 2 spans Kartik through Poush, quarter 3 covers Magh through Chaitra, and quarter 4 spans Baisakh through Ashadh.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

```javascript
const { NepaliDate } = require("nepali-date-library");
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
getCurrentFiscalYearQuarter(): number;
```

---

## Parameters

* None.

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `number`
* **Values**: `1 | 2 | 3 | 4`

| Month (Bikram Sambat) | Month Index | Returned Quarter |
| :--- | :---: | :---: |
| Shrawan, Bhadra, Ashwin | `3`, `4`, `5` | `1` (Q1) |
| Kartik, Mangsir, Poush | `6`, `7`, `8` | `2` (Q2) |
| Magh, Falgun, Chaitra | `9`, `10`, `11` | `3` (Q3) |
| Baisakh, Jestha, Ashadh | `0`, `1`, `2` | `4` (Q4) |

---

## Examples

### Determining Quarter of a Given Date

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const dashainDate = new NepaliDate("2081-07-15"); // Kartik
console.log(dashainDate.getCurrentFiscalYearQuarter()); // 2 (Q2)

const endOfYearDate = new NepaliDate("2081-03-25"); // Ashadh
console.log(endOfYearDate.getCurrentFiscalYearQuarter()); // 4 (Q4)
```

### Financial Audit Filter

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

interface JournalEntry {
  description: string;
  date: NepaliDate;
  amount: number;
}

function filterByFiscalQuarter(entries: JournalEntry[], targetQuarter: number) {
  return entries.filter(
    (entry) => entry.date.getCurrentFiscalYearQuarter() === targetQuarter
  );
}
```

## Page: date.getCurrentFiscalYearQuarterDates() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/fiscal-year/get-current-fiscal-year-quarter-dates)
Description: [NodeJS] Method to retrieve exact start and end boundary dates for the active fiscal quarter. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `getCurrentFiscalYearQuarterDates` method computes the exact starting date and ending date for the fiscal quarter containing the current date instance. It returns an object containing boundary dates as new NepaliDate objects, which is helpful for quarterly financial reporting, audit periods, and tax filing windows.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

```javascript
const { NepaliDate } = require("nepali-date-library");
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
getCurrentFiscalYearQuarterDates(): { start: NepaliDate; end: NepaliDate };
```

---

## Parameters

* None.

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `{ start: NepaliDate; end: NepaliDate }`
* **Structure**:
  * `start`: `NepaliDate` instance pointing to the first day of the quarter at `00:00:00.000`.
  * `end`: `NepaliDate` instance pointing to the final day of the quarter at `23:59:59.999`.

---

## Examples

### Getting Current Quarter Boundaries

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// Assuming today is 2081 Kartik 15 (Q2):
const today = new NepaliDate();
const { start, end } = today.getCurrentFiscalYearQuarterDates();

console.log(start.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2081-07-01" (1 Kartik)
console.log(end.format("YYYY-MM-DD"));   // "2081-09-30" (Last day of Poush)
```

### Database Query Boundary Filter

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

function getActiveQuarterFilter() {
  const now = new NepaliDate();
  const { start, end } = now.getCurrentFiscalYearQuarterDates();

  return {
    startGregorian: start.getEnglishDate(),
    endGregorian: end.getEnglishDate(),
    quarterIndex: now.getCurrentFiscalYearQuarter(),
  };
}
```

## Page: NepaliDate.getFiscalYearQuarter() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/fiscal-year/get-fiscal-year-quarter)
Description: [NodeJS] Static method to determine the fiscal trimester number for any specified month index. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The static `getFiscalYearQuarter` method determines the fiscal trimester number corresponding to a given Bikram Sambat month index from 0 to 11. It allows quick lookups without needing to instantiate a full NepaliDate object, making it useful in financial aggregation pipelines and reporting utilities.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

```javascript
const { NepaliDate } = require("nepali-date-library");
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
static getFiscalYearQuarter(
  quarter: number,
  fiscalYear?: number
): { start: NepaliDate; end: NepaliDate };
```

---

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `quarter` | `number` | Yes | - | Fiscal quarter index (`1`, `2`, `3`, or `4`). |
| `fiscalYear` | `number` | No | Current FY | Base Bikram Sambat year of the fiscal cycle. |

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `{ start: NepaliDate; end: NepaliDate }`
* **Properties**:
  * `start`: `NepaliDate` initialized to day 1 of the quarter's opening month.
  * `end`: `NepaliDate` initialized to the final day of the quarter's closing month at `23:59:59.999`.

---

## Exceptions

| Error Message | Trigger Condition |
| :--- | :--- |
| `Quarter must be an integer between 1 and 4` | Thrown if `quarter` is not an integer or is outside `1` to `4`. |

---

## Examples

### Querying Specific Quarter for Current Fiscal Year

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// Get Q1 of the current fiscal year
const q1 = NepaliDate.getFiscalYearQuarter(1);
console.log(q1.start.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2081-04-01" (1 Shrawan)
console.log(q1.end.format("YYYY-MM-DD"));   // "2081-06-30" (End of Ashwin)
```

### Querying Cross-Year Quarter (Q4)

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// Q4 of FY 2080/81 takes place in calendar year 2081
const q4 = NepaliDate.getFiscalYearQuarter(4, 2080);
console.log(q4.start.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2081-01-01" (1 Baisakh 2081)
console.log(q4.end.format("YYYY-MM-DD"));   // "2081-03-31" (End of Ashadh 2081)
```

## Related

* [`NepaliDate.getFiscalYearQuarters()`](/docs/nodejs/fiscal-year/get-fiscal-year-quarters): Returns all four quarters in one call.
* [`NepaliDate.getCurrentFiscalYear()`](/docs/nodejs/fiscal-year/get-current-fiscal-year): Returns current fiscal year integer.

## Page: NepaliDate.getFiscalYearQuarters() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/fiscal-year/get-fiscal-year-quarters)
Description: [NodeJS] Static utility returning all four fiscal trimesters with their constituent months and date ranges for a given year. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The static `getFiscalYearQuarters` method returns a complete structural breakdown of all four fiscal trimesters for a specified Bikram Sambat year. Each quarter entry includes its trimester index, English and Nepali month names, and corresponding calendar boundary information.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

```javascript
const { NepaliDate } = require("nepali-date-library");
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
static getFiscalYearQuarters(fiscalYear?: number): {
  Q1: { start: NepaliDate; end: NepaliDate };
  Q2: { start: NepaliDate; end: NepaliDate };
  Q3: { start: NepaliDate; end: NepaliDate };
  Q4: { start: NepaliDate; end: NepaliDate };
};
```

---

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `fiscalYear` | `number` | No | Current FY | Base Bikram Sambat year of the fiscal cycle (e.g. `2081`). |

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: An object with keys `Q1`, `Q2`, `Q3`, and `Q4`.
* **Structure**:
  * `Q1`: 1 Shrawan – Last day of Ashwin
  * `Q2`: 1 Kartik – Last day of Poush
  * `Q3`: 1 Magh – Last day of Chaitra
  * `Q4`: 1 Baisakh – Last day of Ashadh (in succeeding calendar year)

---

## Examples

### Getting Current Fiscal Year Quarters

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const quarters = NepaliDate.getFiscalYearQuarters();

console.log("Q1 Start:", quarters.Q1.start.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // 2081-04-01
console.log("Q1 End:  ", quarters.Q1.end.format("YYYY-MM-DD"));   // 2081-06-30
console.log("Q2 Start:", quarters.Q2.start.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // 2081-07-01
console.log("Q2 End:  ", quarters.Q2.end.format("YYYY-MM-DD"));   // 2081-09-30
console.log("Q3 Start:", quarters.Q3.start.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // 2081-10-01
console.log("Q3 End:  ", quarters.Q3.end.format("YYYY-MM-DD"));   // 2081-12-30
console.log("Q4 Start:", quarters.Q4.start.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // 2082-01-01
console.log("Q4 End:  ", quarters.Q4.end.format("YYYY-MM-DD"));   // 2082-03-31
```

### Iterating for Financial Charts

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const quarters = NepaliDate.getFiscalYearQuarters(2080);

const quarterList = Object.entries(quarters).map(([quarterName, dates]) => ({
  quarter: quarterName,
  startDateBS: dates.start.format("YYYY-MM-DD"),
  endDateBS: dates.end.format("YYYY-MM-DD"),
  startDateAD: dates.start.getEnglishDate().toISOString().split("T")[0],
  endDateAD: dates.end.getEnglishDate().toISOString().split("T")[0],
}));

console.log(quarterList);
```

Description: [NodeJS] Installation and setup guide for the nepali date library in Node.js and TypeScript applications using standard package managers. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The nepali date library is distributed as a lightweight npm package compatible with modern JavaScript runtimes including Node.js, Bun, and Deno. It provides native TypeScript type definitions out of the box with zero runtime dependencies, making setup fast across all standard package managers.

## Import Syntax

The package supports both ECMAScript Modules (ESM) and CommonJS (CJS) natively.

### ECMAScript Modules (TypeScript / Modern JS)

// or default import

### CommonJS

```javascript
const { NepaliDate, ADtoBS, BStoAD } = require("nepali-date-library");

// or default require

```

---

## TypeScript Configuration

`nepali-date-library` is written in TypeScript and ships with bundled type definitions (`.d.ts`). No additional `@types/` packages are required.

Recommended `tsconfig.json` compiler options:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2020",
    "module": "NodeNext",
    "moduleResolution": "NodeNext",
    "strict": true,
    "esModuleInterop": true
  }
}
```

---

## Zero Dependencies

The package has **0 runtime external dependencies**. It contains all astronomical calendar mappings, formatting tokens, and date arithmetic routines internally, guaranteeing small bundle size and zero transitive vulnerability risks.

## Page: date.addDays() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/add-days)
Description: [NodeJS] Add or subtract a specified number of days to a NepaliDate instance with automatic month and year rollover. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `addDays` method modifies the current `NepaliDate` instance by adding or subtracting a given integer number of days. It automatically handles variable Bikram Sambat month day counts, transitions across month boundaries, and advances or decrements the year when needed.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
addDays(days: number): NepaliDate;
```

---

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- |
| `days` | `number` | Yes | Integer number of days to add (positive) or subtract (negative). |

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `NepaliDate`
* Returns a new `NepaliDate` instance with the specified days added or subtracted. The original instance is not modified.

---

## Examples

### Adding Days Across Month Boundaries

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// 2081 Baisakh 25 (Baisakh 2081 has 31 days)
const date = new NepaliDate("2081-01-25");

const next = date.addDays(10);
console.log(next.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2081-02-04" (4 Jestha)
```

### Subtracting Days Across Year Boundaries

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// 2081 Baisakh 02
const date = new NepaliDate("2081-01-02");

const prev = date.addDays(-5);
console.log(prev.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2080-12-28" (28 Chaitra 2080)
```

### Method Chaining

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date = new NepaliDate("2081-01-01")
  .addDays(15)
  .addDays(5);

console.log(date.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2081-01-21"
```

---

* [`date.addMonths()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/add-months): Add or subtract whole months.
* [`date.diff()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/diff): Calculate the difference between two dates in days.

## Page: date.addMonths() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/add-months)
Description: [NodeJS] Add or subtract months to a NepaliDate instance while adjusting for variable month lengths. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `addMonths` method advances or rewinds the current `NepaliDate` instance by a specified number of months. If the current day of the month exceeds the total days available in the destination month, the method automatically clamps the day to the final valid day of that month to ensure calendar consistency.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
addMonths(months: number): NepaliDate;
```

---

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- |
| `months` | `number` | Yes | Number of months to add (positive) or subtract (negative). |

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `NepaliDate`
* Returns a new `NepaliDate` instance with the added or subtracted months. The original instance is not modified.

---

## Exceptions

Throws an `Error` if the resulting year falls outside the supported Bikram Sambat calendar range (1976 BS to 2100 BS):

```typescript
"Resulting date is out of supported range"
```

---

## Examples

### Adding Months Within the Same Year

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// 2081 Baisakh 15 (month index 0)
const date = new NepaliDate(2081, 0, 15);

const future = date.addMonths(3);
console.log(future.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2081-04-15" (Shrawan)
```

### Day Clamping on Shorter Months

When transitioning into a month with fewer days, the day component automatically adjusts to the maximum valid day of that target month:

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// 2081 Baisakh 31 (Baisakh has 31 days)
const date = new NepaliDate(2081, 0, 31);

// Jestha 2081 has 32 days -> day remains 31
const jestha = date.addMonths(1);
console.log(jestha.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2081-02-31"

// Kartik 2081 has 30 days -> day is clamped to 30
const kartik = date.addMonths(6);
console.log(kartik.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2081-07-30"
```

### Subtracting Months Across Year Boundaries

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// 2081 Baisakh 10
const date = new NepaliDate(2081, 0, 10);

const past = date.addMonths(-2);
console.log(past.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2080-11-10" (Falgun 2080)
```

* [`date.diff()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/diff): Calculate differences between two dates.

## Page: date.addYears() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/add-years)
Description: [NodeJS] Add or subtract years to a NepaliDate instance while preserving month and day values. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `addYears` method adds or subtracts a specified number of years to the current `NepaliDate` instance. It recalculates the underlying timestamp while retaining the month and day coordinates, adjusting the day number if the target year has fewer days in that specific month.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
addYears(years: number): NepaliDate;
```

---

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- |
| `years` | `number` | Yes | Number of years to add (positive) or subtract (negative). |

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `NepaliDate`
* Returns a new `NepaliDate` instance with the added or subtracted years. The original instance is not modified.

---

## Exceptions

Throws an `Error` if the resulting year falls outside the supported Bikram Sambat calendar range (1976 BS to 2100 BS):

```typescript
"Resulting date is out of supported range"
```

---

## Examples

### Adding and Subtracting Years

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date = new NepaliDate("2081-05-15");

const future = date.addYears(5);
console.log(future.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2086-05-15"

const past = date.addYears(-10);
console.log(past.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2071-05-15"
```

### Day Clamping on Variable Month Lengths

Because month lengths in the Bikram Sambat astronomical calendar vary across years, `addYears()` automatically clamps the day component if the destination year has fewer days in that month:

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// 2081 Baisakh 31 (Baisakh 2081 has 31 days)
const date = new NepaliDate(2081, 0, 31);

// If Baisakh in a target year has only 30 days, day clamps to 30
const nextYear = date.addYears(1);
console.log(nextYear.getDate()); // Clamped to valid range
```

## Page: date.clone() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/clone)
Description: [NodeJS] Create an independent deep clone of an existing NepaliDate instance. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `clone` method creates and returns an independent duplicate of the current `NepaliDate` instance. Because several library arithmetic and mutation methods alter instances in place, creating a clone allows you to perform calculations without modifying the original date object.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
clone(): NepaliDate;
```

---

## Parameters

This method does not take any parameters.

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `NepaliDate`
* Returns a new independent `NepaliDate` instance initialized with the exact state of the current instance.

---

## Examples

### Creating an Independent Duplicate

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const original = new NepaliDate("2081-01-15");
const duplicate = original.clone();

// Mutating duplicate does not impact original
duplicate.setDate(20);

console.log(original.format("YYYY-MM-DD"));  // "2081-01-15"
console.log(duplicate.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2081-01-20"
```

## Page: date.daysInMonth() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/days-in-month)
Description: [NodeJS] Retrieve the total number of days in the current or specified Bikram Sambat month. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `daysInMonth` method returns the total number of days present in the active month of the current `NepaliDate` instance, or for an explicitly provided year and month combination. Because Bikram Sambat month durations vary from 29 to 32 days depending on astronomical solar calculations, this method provides accurate month lengths.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
daysInMonth(year?: number, month?: number): number;
```

---

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| `year` | `number` | No | `this.year` | Bikram Sambat year (e.g. `2081`). |
| `month` | `number` | No | `this.month` | Zero-indexed month (`0-11`, where `0` is Baisakh and `11` is Chaitra). |

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `number`
* The number of days in the specified month (typically between 29 and 32 days).

---

## Exceptions

Throws an `Error` if `month` is explicitly provided and is less than 0 or greater than 11:

```typescript
"Invalid month index, must be between 0-11"
```

---

## Examples

### Querying the Current Instance Month

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// 2081 Baisakh
const date = new NepaliDate(2081, 0, 15);
console.log(date.daysInMonth()); // 31
```

### Querying an Arbitrary Year and Month

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date = new NepaliDate();

// Querying Jestha 2081 (month index 1)
const jesthaDays = date.daysInMonth(2081, 1);
console.log(jesthaDays); // 32

// Querying Chaitra 2080 (month index 11)
const chaitraDays = date.daysInMonth(2080, 11);
console.log(chaitraDays); // 30
```

## Page: date.diff() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/diff)
Description: [NodeJS] Calculate the chronological difference between two NepaliDate instances in specific time units. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `diff` method calculates the elapsed time duration between the current `NepaliDate` instance and another date object. It can return the difference in days, months, years, hours, minutes, seconds, or milliseconds, making it suitable for calculating age, tenure, or interval durations.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
diff(date: NepaliDate, unit: "year" | "month" | "day"): number;
```

---

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- |
| `date` | `NepaliDate` | Yes | The target `NepaliDate` instance to compare against. |
| `unit` | `"year" \| "month" \| "day"` | Yes | The unit of measurement for the difference calculation. |

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `number`
* The numeric difference between the two dates (`this - date`).
* Positive if the current date is after `date`.
* Negative if the current date is before `date`.
* Zero if they are identical in the evaluated unit.

---

## Calculation Rules

* **`"day"`**: Computed using Unix timestamps: `Math.floor((this.getTime() - date.getTime()) / 86400000)`.
* **`"month"`**: Computed using calendar month indices: `(this.year - date.year) * 12 + (this.month - date.month)`.
* **`"year"`**: Computed by year difference: `this.year - date.year`.

---

## Exceptions

Throws an `Error` if an invalid unit string is supplied:

```typescript
"Invalid unit for diff calculation"
```

---

## Examples

### Difference in Days

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date1 = new NepaliDate("2081-01-20");
const date2 = new NepaliDate("2081-01-05");

console.log(date1.diff(date2, "day")); // 15
console.log(date2.diff(date1, "day")); // -15
```

### Difference in Months

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date1 = new NepaliDate("2081-06-15");
const date2 = new NepaliDate("2080-04-15");

console.log(date1.diff(date2, "month")); // 14
```

### Difference in Years

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date1 = new NepaliDate("2085-01-01");
const date2 = new NepaliDate("2081-01-01");

console.log(date1.diff(date2, "year")); // 4
```

## Page: date.endOfDay() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/end-of-day)
Description: [NodeJS] Return a new NepaliDate instance set to the final millisecond of the current day. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `endOfDay` method returns a new `NepaliDate` instance with time coordinates set to the final moment of the day at 23 hours, 59 minutes, 59 seconds, and 999 milliseconds. This is commonly used when setting upper boundaries for database queries, event schedules, and daily audit filters.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
endOfDay(): NepaliDate;
```

---

## Parameters

This method does not take any parameters.

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `NepaliDate`
* Returns a new cloned `NepaliDate` instance set to `23:59:59.999` on the same calendar day. The original instance is not modified.

---

## Examples

### Generating End-of-Day Timestamp

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date = new NepaliDate("2081-05-15");
const end = date.endOfDay();

console.log(end.getHours()); // 23
console.log(end.getMinutes()); // 59
console.log(end.getSeconds()); // 59
console.log(end.getMilliseconds()); // 999
```

### Inclusive Day Range Filtering

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// Set upper bound for date filters
const reportDate = new NepaliDate("2081-01-31").endOfDay();

console.log(reportDate.getTime()); // Unix timestamp in milliseconds
```

## Page: date.endOfMonth() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/end-of-month)
Description: [NodeJS] Return a new NepaliDate instance set to the final day of the current Bikram Sambat month. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `endOfMonth` method returns a new `NepaliDate` instance positioned on the last valid calendar day of the active month. It automatically checks the calendar map to determine whether the month ends on day 29, 30, 31, or 32, which is useful for monthly reporting and billing cycles.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
endOfMonth(): NepaliDate;
```

---

## Parameters

This method does not take any parameters.

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `NepaliDate`
* Returns a new `NepaliDate` set to the last calendar day of the month at `23:59:59.999`. The original instance is not modified.

---

## Examples

### Determining Last Day of the Month

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// 2081 Baisakh (which has 31 days)
const date = new NepaliDate(2081, 0, 10);

const lastDay = date.endOfMonth();
console.log(lastDay.getDate()); // 31
console.log(lastDay.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2081-01-31"
console.log(lastDay.getHours()); // 23
console.log(lastDay.getMinutes()); // 59
```

### Variable Month Ends Across Years

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// 2080 Chaitra has 30 days
const chaitra2080 = new NepaliDate(2080, 11, 1).endOfMonth();
console.log(chaitra2080.getDate()); // 30

// 2081 Chaitra has 30 days
const chaitra2081 = new NepaliDate(2081, 11, 1).endOfMonth();
console.log(chaitra2081.getDate()); // 30
```

## Page: date.endOfWeek() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/end-of-week)
Description: [NodeJS] Return a new NepaliDate instance set to the final day of the current week on Saturday. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `endOfWeek` method produces a new `NepaliDate` instance representing the last day of the week containing the current date. In standard Nepali calendar practice, Saturday is regarded as the final day of the weekly cycle.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
endOfWeek(startOfWeek?: number): NepaliDate;
```

---

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| `startOfWeek` | `number` | No | `0` | Day of week index (`0-6`) that defines when the week begins. By default, `0` (Sunday) is the start, making Saturday (6) the end. |

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `NepaliDate`
* Returns a new `NepaliDate` instance set to the end of the final day of the week (`23:59:59.999`). The original instance is not modified.

---

## Exceptions

Throws an `Error` if `startOfWeek` is not an integer between `0` and `6`:

```typescript
"startOfWeek must be an integer between 0 and 6"
```

---

## Examples

### Default Week End (Saturday 23:59:59)

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date = new NepaliDate("2081-02-16");

const weekEnd = date.endOfWeek();
console.log(weekEnd.getDay()); // 6 (Saturday)
console.log(weekEnd.getHours()); // 23
console.log(weekEnd.getMinutes()); // 59
```

### Custom Week Ending on Sunday

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date = new NepaliDate("2081-02-16");

// Week starts on Monday (1), meaning it ends on Sunday (0)
const weekEnd = date.endOfWeek(1);
console.log(weekEnd.getDay()); // 0 (Sunday)
```

---

## Related

* [`date.endOfDay()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/end-of-day): Return end of the day.

## Page: date.endOfYear() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/end-of-year)
Description: [NodeJS] Return a new NepaliDate instance set to the final day of the Bikram Sambat year on the last day of Chaitra. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `endOfYear` method returns a new `NepaliDate` instance set to the closing day of the current Bikram Sambat calendar year. This corresponds to the final day of Chaitra, which is commonly needed for annual reconciliations and fiscal year preparations.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
endOfYear(): NepaliDate;
```

---

## Parameters

This method does not take any parameters.

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `NepaliDate`
* Returns a new `NepaliDate` set to the last day of Chaitra for the given year at `23:59:59.999`. The original instance is not modified.

---

## Examples

### Getting the Final Day of the Calendar Year

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date = new NepaliDate("2081-03-15");

const yearEnd = date.endOfYear();
console.log(yearEnd.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2081-12-30"
console.log(yearEnd.getMonth()); // 11 (Chaitra)
console.log(yearEnd.getHours()); // 23
console.log(yearEnd.getMinutes()); // 59
console.log(yearEnd.getSeconds()); // 59
```

### Full Calendar Year Span

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const year = 2081;
const start = new NepaliDate(year, 0, 1).startOfDay();
const end = new NepaliDate(year, 0, 1).endOfYear();

console.log(`Year ${year} spans from ${start.format("YYYY-MM-DD")} to ${end.format("YYYY-MM-DD")}`);
```

* [`date.endOfMonth()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/end-of-month): Return the final day of the current month.
* [`date.isLeapYear()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/is-leap-year): Check if the year has 366 days.

## Page: date.format() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/format)
Description: [NodeJS] Format a NepaliDate instance into a custom string using token patterns for English and Nepali output. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `format` method transforms a `NepaliDate` instance into a formatted string according to a pattern of token specifiers. It supports tokens for year, month, day, weekday, hours, minutes, and seconds, with full support for localized English names as well as Devanagari script numerals and words.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
format(formatStr: string): string;
```

---

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- |
| `formatStr` | `string` | Yes | Formatting template string containing pattern tokens. |

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `string`
* The formatted date string with all tokens substituted.

---

## Token Reference

Uppercase characters produce English representations, while lowercase characters produce Devanagari (Nepali) representations.

### Year Tokens

| Token | Output | Description | Example (2081 BS) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `YYYY` | English 4-digit year | Full Gregorian-style digit year | `"2081"` |
| `YYY` | English 3-digit year | Last 3 digits | `"081"` |
| `YY` | English 2-digit year | Last 2 digits | `"81"` |
| `yyyy` | Nepali 4-digit year | Devanagari numerals | `"२०८१"` |
| `yyy` | Nepali 3-digit year | Last 3 digits in Devanagari | `"०८१"` |
| `yy` | Nepali 2-digit year | Last 2 digits in Devanagari | `"८१"` |

### Month Tokens

| Token | Output | Description | Example (Baisakh) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `M` | English 1-digit | Month number (`1-12`) | `"1"` |
| `MM` | English 2-digit | Zero-padded month number (`01-12`) | `"01"` |
| `MMM` | English 3-letter | Abbreviated month name | `"Bai"` |
| `MMMM` | English Full | Complete romanized month name | `"Baisakh"` |
| `m` | Nepali 1-digit | Devanagari month number (`१-१२`) | `"१"` |
| `mm` | Nepali 2-digit | Zero-padded Devanagari month number | `"०१"` |
| `mmm` | Nepali Short | Abbreviated Devanagari month name | `"बै"` |
| `mmmm` | Nepali Full | Complete Devanagari month name | `"बैशाख"` |

### Day and Weekday Tokens

| Token | Output | Description | Example (Day 5, Sunday) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `D` | English 1-digit | Day of the month (`1-32`) | `"5"` |
| `DD` | English 2-digit | Zero-padded day of the month (`01-32`) | `"05"` |
| `DDD` | English Short | Abbreviated weekday name | `"Sun"` |
| `DDDD` | English Full | Complete weekday name | `"Sunday"` |
| `d` | Nepali 1-digit | Devanagari day of the month (`१-३२`) | `"५"` |
| `dd` | Nepali 2-digit | Zero-padded Devanagari day of the month | `"०५"` |
| `ddd` | Nepali Short | Abbreviated Devanagari weekday | `"आइत"` |
| `dddd` | Nepali Full | Complete Devanagari weekday | `"आइतबार"` |

---

## Escaping Literal Characters

To include literal characters that conflict with format tokens (such as `M`, `D`, `Y`, `m`, `d`, `y`), wrap the text inside double quotes (`"`):

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date = new NepaliDate("2081-01-25");

const formatted = date.format('"Date:" YYYY-MM-DD');
console.log(formatted); // 'Date: 2081-01-25'
```

---

## Examples

### Standard ISO-Style Formatting

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date = new NepaliDate("2081-01-05");

console.log(date.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2081-01-05"
console.log(date.format("YYYY/MM/DD")); // "2081/01/05"
```

### Full English Date with Weekday

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date = new NepaliDate("2081-01-25");

console.log(date.format("DDDD, MMMM DD, YYYY"));
// "Thursday, Baisakh 25, 2081"
```

### Native Nepali Devanagari Formatting

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date = new NepaliDate("2081-01-25");

console.log(date.format("dddd, mmmm dd, yyyy"));
// "बिहिबार, बैशाख २५, २०८१"

console.log(date.format("yyyy-mm-dd"));
// "२०८१-०१-२५"
```
