## Page: date.getCurrentQuarter() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/get-current-quarter)
Description: [NodeJS] Return the standard Bikram Sambat calendar quarter number from one to four for the current date. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `getCurrentQuarter` method returns an integer from 1 to 4 designating the standard calendar quarter containing the current date. Calendar quarters divide the Bikram Sambat year into four sequential segments starting from 1 Baisakh, which differs from government fiscal trimesters that commence in Shrawan.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
getCurrentQuarter(): number;
```

---

## Parameters

This method does not take any parameters.

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `number`
* The calendar quarter integer (`1`, `2`, `3`, or `4`):
  * `1`: Baisakh, Jestha, Asar (Months `0-2`)
  * `2`: Shrawan, Bhadra, Aswin (Months `3-5`)
  * `3`: Kartik, Mangsir, Poush (Months `6-8`)
  * `4`: Magh, Falgun, Chaitra (Months `9-11`)

---

## Note on Fiscal Quarters

Calendar quarters follow the Baisakh-to-Chaitra annual cycle. If you require Government of Nepal / IRD fiscal quarters (which begin in Shrawan), use [`date.getCurrentFiscalYearQuarter()`](/docs/nodejs/fiscal-year/get-current-fiscal-year-quarter) instead.

---

## Examples

### Determining Current Calendar Quarter

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// 2081 Baisakh 15 (month index 0)
const date1 = new NepaliDate(2081, 0, 15);
console.log(date1.getCurrentQuarter()); // 1

// 2081 Shrawan 1 (month index 3)
const date2 = new NepaliDate(2081, 3, 1);
console.log(date2.getCurrentQuarter()); // 2

// 2081 Kartik 10 (month index 6)
const date3 = new NepaliDate(2081, 6, 10);
console.log(date3.getCurrentQuarter()); // 3

// 2081 Magh 20 (month index 9)
const date4 = new NepaliDate(2081, 9, 20);
console.log(date4.getCurrentQuarter()); // 4
```

---

## Related

* [`NepaliDate.getQuarter()`](/docs/nodejs/fiscal-year/calendar-quarters): Get start and end dates for a specific calendar quarter.
* [`date.getCurrentFiscalYearQuarter()`](/docs/nodejs/fiscal-year/get-current-fiscal-year-quarter): Get the Nepali fiscal quarter (`1-4`).

## Page: date.getEnglishDate() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/get-english-date)
Description: [NodeJS] Retrieve the equivalent Gregorian date as a native JavaScript Date object. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `getEnglishDate` method returns the native JavaScript Date object corresponding to the current `NepaliDate` instance. This allows seamless integration with third party libraries, databases, and standard browser APIs that expect a native Gregorian Date object.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
getEnglishDate(): Date;
```

---

## Parameters

* None.

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `Date`
* **Description**: A standard JavaScript `Date` instance calibrated in UTC.

---

## Examples

### Converting to Native JavaScript Date

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const nepaliDate = new NepaliDate("2081-07-15");
const jsDate = nepaliDate.getEnglishDate();

console.log(jsDate instanceof Date); // true
console.log(jsDate.toISOString()); // "2024-10-31T00:00:00.000Z"
console.log(jsDate.getUTCFullYear()); // 2024
console.log(jsDate.getUTCMonth()); // 9 (October, 0-indexed)
console.log(jsDate.getUTCDate()); // 31
```

### Passing to Third-Party Date Utilities

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date = new NepaliDate("2081-01-01");
const englishDate = date.getEnglishDate();

// Interoperable with Intl.DateTimeFormat or external libraries
const formatted = new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", {
  dateStyle: "full",
  timeZone: "UTC",
}).format(englishDate);

console.log(formatted); // "Saturday, April 13, 2024"
```

## Page: date.getMonth() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/get-month)
Description: [NodeJS] Retrieve the zero based Bikram Sambat month index from zero for Baisakh to eleven for Chaitra. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `getMonth` method returns the month of the year as an integer between 0 and 11 for the current `NepaliDate` instance. The library adheres to the JavaScript zero based indexing standard where 0 represents Baisakh, 1 represents Jestha, and 11 represents Chaitra.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
getMonth(): number;
```

---

## Parameters

* None.

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `number`
* **Range**: `0` to `11`

| Index | Month (English) | Month (Devanagari) |
| :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `0` | Baisakh | बैशाख |
| `1` | Jestha | जेठ |
| `2` | Ashadh / Asar | असार |
| `3` | Shrawan | श्रावण |
| `4` | Bhadra | भाद्र |
| `5` | Ashwin / Aswin | आश्विन |
| `6` | Kartik | कार्तिक |
| `7` | Mangsir | मंसिर |
| `8` | Poush | पौष |
| `9` | Magh | माघ |
| `10` | Falgun | फाल्गुण |
| `11` | Chaitra | चैत्र |

---

## Example

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// 2081 Kartik 15
const date = new NepaliDate("2081-07-15");

console.log(date.getMonth()); // 6 (0-indexed)
console.log(date.getMonth() + 1); // 7 (1-indexed for display)
```

## Page: date.getTime() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/get-time)
Description: [NodeJS] Retrieve the numeric timestamp in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `getTime` method returns the number of milliseconds elapsed since the Unix epoch of January 1, 1970 UTC. This integer value matches the return value of native JavaScript Date getTime and allows direct numerical comparison between date instances.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
getTime(): number;
```

---

## Parameters

* None.

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `number`
* **Description**: Integer representing milliseconds since January 1, 1970 UTC.

---

## Examples

### Getting Unix Epoch Timestamp

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date = new NepaliDate("2081-07-15");
console.log(date.getTime()); // 1730332800000
```

### Direct Mathematical Timestamp Comparison

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date1 = new NepaliDate("2081-01-01");
const date2 = new NepaliDate("2081-02-01");

const diffMs = date2.getTime() - date1.getTime();
const diffDays = diffMs / (1000 * 60 * 60 * 24);
console.log(diffDays); // 31
```

## Page: date.getWeeksInMonth() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/get-weeks-in-month)
Description: [NodeJS] Calculate the number of calendar week rows required to render the current month in a grid. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `getWeeksInMonth` method computes the total number of seven day week rows required to display the entire month in a standard calendar grid. Depending on which weekday the month starts on and how many days it contains, the returned count is usually five or six rows.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
getWeeksInMonth(): number;
```

---

## Parameters

This method does not take any parameters.

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `number`
* The number of calendar week rows needed (typically `5` or `6`).

---

## Formula

The calculation evaluates the weekday offset of the 1st of the month added to the month's total days, divided by 7:

```typescript
Math.ceil((firstDayOfWeek + totalDays) / 7)
```

---

## Examples

### Sizing UI Calendar Views

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date = new NepaliDate("2081-01-15");
const rowCount = date.getWeeksInMonth();

console.log(`Calendar requires ${rowCount} week rows.`);
```

## Page: date.isAfter() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/is-after)
Description: [NodeJS] Check whether the current date occurs chronologically after another specified date. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `isAfter` method evaluates whether the current `NepaliDate` instance occurs chronologically later than another date or timestamp. It compares exact millisecond values to determine chronological order accurately.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
isAfter(date: NepaliDate): boolean;
```

---

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- |
| `date` | `NepaliDate` | Yes | Target `NepaliDate` instance to compare against. |

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `boolean`
* Returns `true` if the current date and time succeeds the provided `date` in absolute time; otherwise returns `false`.

---

## Precision

Comparison is evaluated down to the exact millisecond using the underlying Unix timestamp:

```typescript
this.timestamp.getTime() > date.timestamp.getTime()
```

---

## Examples

### Chronological Comparison

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const releaseDate = new NepaliDate("2081-05-01");
const currentDate = new NepaliDate("2081-06-10");

console.log(currentDate.isAfter(releaseDate)); // true
console.log(releaseDate.isAfter(currentDate)); // false
```

### Checking Expiration or Deadlines

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const deadline = new NepaliDate("2081-02-30").endOfDay();
const submission = new NepaliDate();

if (submission.isAfter(deadline)) {
  console.log("Submission window has closed.");
}
```

---

* [`date.isEqual()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/is-equal): Check if calendar dates are identical.
* [`date.isSame()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/is-same): Check equality by specific unit.

## Page: date.isBefore() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/is-before)
Description: [NodeJS] Check whether the current date occurs chronologically before another specified date. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `isBefore` method evaluates whether the current `NepaliDate` instance occurs earlier in time than another provided date. It takes into account both date and time components down to millisecond accuracy.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
isBefore(date: NepaliDate): boolean;
```

---

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- |
| `date` | `NepaliDate` | Yes | Target `NepaliDate` instance to compare against. |

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `boolean`
* Returns `true` if the current date and time precedes the provided `date` in absolute time; otherwise returns `false`.

---

## Precision

Comparison is evaluated down to the exact millisecond using the underlying Unix timestamp:

```typescript
this.timestamp.getTime() < date.timestamp.getTime()
```

---

## Examples

### Chronological Comparison

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date1 = new NepaliDate("2081-01-15");
const date2 = new NepaliDate("2081-01-20");

console.log(date1.isBefore(date2)); // true
console.log(date2.isBefore(date1)); // false
```

### Time-Level Comparison

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const morning = new NepaliDate("2081-01-15").startOfDay();
const evening = new NepaliDate("2081-01-15").endOfDay();

console.log(morning.isBefore(evening)); // true
```

## Page: date.isEqual() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/is-equal)
Description: [NodeJS] Check whether two date instances share the exact same calendar date coordinates regardless of time. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `isEqual` method checks whether the current `NepaliDate` instance shares the exact same Bikram Sambat year, month, and day coordinates as another date object, ignoring any differences in hours, minutes, seconds, or milliseconds.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
isEqual(date: NepaliDate): boolean;
```

---

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- |
| `date` | `NepaliDate` | Yes | Target `NepaliDate` instance to compare against. |

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `boolean`
* Returns `true` if `year`, `month`, and `day` are identical; otherwise returns `false`.

---

## Behavior Note

Unlike `isBefore()` and `isAfter()`, which compare millisecond-level timestamps, `isEqual()` evaluates calendar dates only:

```typescript
this.year === date.year && this.month === date.month && this.day === date.day
```

Two instances created at different times of the same day will return `true`.

---

## Examples

### Comparing Calendar Dates

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date1 = new NepaliDate("2081-01-15");
const date2 = new NepaliDate(2081, 0, 15);

console.log(date1.isEqual(date2)); // true
```

### Time Component Independence

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const morning = new NepaliDate("2081-01-15").startOfDay();
const evening = new NepaliDate("2081-01-15").endOfDay();

console.log(morning.isEqual(evening)); // true
```

---

## Related

* [`date.isSame()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/is-same): Compare dates by specific calendar unit (`year`, `month`, or `day`).
* [`date.isBefore()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/is-before): Millisecond-level chronological check.
* [`date.isAfter()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/is-after): Millisecond-level chronological check.

## Page: date.isLeapYear() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/is-leap-year)
Description: [NodeJS] Determine whether the current Bikram Sambat calendar year has three hundred sixty six or more days. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `isLeapYear` method checks whether the active Bikram Sambat year contains 366 or more days based on official solar calendar tables. Because Bikram Sambat year lengths depend on astronomical calculations rather than fixed leap year cycles, this method checks the actual cumulative day count for the year.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
isLeapYear(): boolean;
```

---

## Parameters

This method does not take any parameters.

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `boolean`
* Returns `true` if the total days in the current Bikram Sambat year is greater than or equal to 366; otherwise returns `false`.

---

## Background

Unlike the Gregorian calendar which inserts a leap day every 4 years on February 29, the Bikram Sambat calendar is a sidereal solar calendar where each month's duration is determined by the exact astrological entry (Sankranti) of the Sun into each zodiac constellation. Consequently, the total number of days in a Bikram Sambat year fluctuates between 365 and 366 days based on astronomical observation data.

---

## Examples

### Checking if a Year is a Leap Year

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date2081 = new NepaliDate("2081-01-01");
console.log(date2081.isLeapYear());

const date2080 = new NepaliDate("2080-01-01");
console.log(date2080.isLeapYear());
```

---

## Related

* [`date.daysInMonth()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/days-in-month): Query days in a specific month.
* [`date.getYear()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/get-year): Retrieve current year.

---

## Page: date.isSame() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/is-same)
Description: [NodeJS] Check whether two dates match across a specified granularity such as year, month, or day. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `isSame` method compares the current `NepaliDate` instance with another date at a specified level of granularity, such as year, month, day, hour, or minute. It returns true if both dates match within that specific unit, simplifying range checks and calendar filters.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
isSame(date: NepaliDate, unit: "year" | "month" | "day"): boolean;
```

---

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- |
| `date` | `NepaliDate` | Yes | Target `NepaliDate` instance to compare against. |
| `unit` | `"year" \| "month" \| "day"` | Yes | Unit of granularity for comparison. |

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `boolean`
* Returns `true` if both dates are identical within the specified unit boundary; otherwise returns `false`.

---

## Comparison Rules

* **`"year"`**: Evaluates `this.year === date.year`.
* **`"month"`**: Evaluates `this.year === date.year && this.month === date.month`.
* **`"day"`**: Evaluates `this.isEqual(date)` (matching year, month, and day).

---

## Exceptions

Throws an `Error` if an invalid unit string is supplied:

```typescript
"Invalid unit for comparison"
```

---

## Examples

### Comparing Same Month

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date1 = new NepaliDate("2081-03-05");
const date2 = new NepaliDate("2081-03-25");
const date3 = new NepaliDate("2080-03-05");

console.log(date1.isSame(date2, "month")); // true (both Ashadh 2081)
console.log(date1.isSame(date3, "month")); // false (different years)
```

### Comparing Same Year

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date1 = new NepaliDate("2081-01-01");
const date2 = new NepaliDate("2081-12-30");

console.log(date1.isSame(date2, "year")); // true
```

### Comparing Same Day

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date1 = new NepaliDate("2081-01-15");
const date2 = new NepaliDate("2081-01-15");

console.log(date1.isSame(date2, "day")); // true
```

---

## Related

* [`date.isEqual()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/is-equal): Strict calendar day equality.
* [`date.diff()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/diff): Measure quantitative difference between dates.

## Page: date.parse() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/parse)
Description: [NodeJS] Parse a formatted Bikram Sambat date string and update the current date instance in place. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `parse` method parses a Bikram Sambat date string and updates the coordinates of the current `NepaliDate` instance in place. It supports various delimiter styles including slashes, dots, and hyphens, recalculating the underlying timestamp upon successful parsing.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
parse(dateString: string): void;
```

---

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- |
| `dateString` | `string` | Yes | Date string formatted as `YYYY-MM-DD`, `YYYY/MM/DD`, or `YYYY.MM.DD`. |

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `void`
* Mutates the current `NepaliDate` instance in place.

---

## Exceptions

| Error Message | Trigger Condition |
| :--- | :--- |
| `Invalid date` | Thrown if string segments are non-numeric. |
| `Nepal year out of range` | Thrown if the parsed year is outside 1976 to 2100 BS. |
| `Invalid nepali month must be between 1 - 12` | Thrown if month is outside `1` to `12`. |
| `Invalid nepali date must be between 1 - <max> in <year> <month>` | Thrown if day exceeds the month's verified length. |

---

## Example

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date = new NepaliDate();

// Mutate instance from string
date.parse("2081-07-15");
console.log(date.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2081-07-15"

// Delimiters with slash or period are supported
date.parse("2082/01/01");
console.log(date.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2082-01-01"
```

---

## Related

* [`new NepaliDate(string)`](/docs/nodejs/class/constructor): Construct a new instance directly from a string.
* [`date.set()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/set): Set coordinates using numeric values.

---

## Page: date.set() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/set)
Description: [NodeJS] Set year, month, and day coordinates simultaneously on a NepaliDate instance. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `set` method updates the Bikram Sambat year, zero based month index, and day values of the current `NepaliDate` instance in a single atomic call. It validates the combined coordinates against the calendar map and recalculates the internal timestamp.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
set(year: number, month: number, date: number): void;
```

---

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- |
| `year` | `number` | Yes | 4-digit Bikram Sambat year (`1976` to `2100`). |
| `month` | `number` | Yes | **0-indexed** month integer (`0` for Baisakh to `11` for Chaitra). |
| `date` | `number` | Yes | Day of the month (`1` to `32`). |

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `void`
* Mutates the current `NepaliDate` instance in place.

---

## Exceptions

| Error Message | Trigger Condition |
| :--- | :--- |
| `Nepal year out of range` | Thrown if `year` is earlier than 1976 BS or later than 2100 BS. |
| `Invalid nepali month must be between 1 - 12` | Thrown if `month` is outside `0` to `11`. |
| `Invalid nepali date must be between 1 - <max> in <year> <month>` | Thrown if `date` exceeds the days count for the target month and year. |

---

## Example

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date = new NepaliDate();

// Mutate to 2081 Kartik 15 (month index 6)
date.set(2081, 6, 15);

console.log(date.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2081-07-15"
console.log(date.getEnglishDate().toISOString()); // "2024-10-31T00:00:00.000Z"
```

---

## Related

* [`date.setYear()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/set-year): Mutate only the year component.
* [`date.setMonth()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/set-month): Mutate only the month component.
* [`date.setDate()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/set-date): Mutate only the day component.

---

## Page: date.setDate() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/set-date)
Description: [NodeJS] Set the day of the month on a NepaliDate instance and recalculate its timestamp. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `setDate` method updates the day of the month for the current `NepaliDate` instance and recalculates its underlying Gregorian timestamp. It validates the new day against the maximum number of days available in the active month.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
setDate(day: number): void;
```

---

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- |
| `day` | `number` | Yes | Day of the month (`1` to `32`, validated against current month's length). |

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `void`
* Mutates the current `NepaliDate` instance in place.

---

## Exceptions

| Error Message | Trigger Condition |
| :--- | :--- |
| `Invalid nepali date must be between 1 - <max> in <year> <month>` | Thrown if `day` is less than `1` or greater than the maximum days in the current month for this year. |

---

## Example

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date = new NepaliDate("2081-01-01");
date.setDate(25);

console.log(date.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2081-01-25"
```

## Page: date.setMonth() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/set-month)
Description: [NodeJS] Set the Bikram Sambat month index on a NepaliDate instance with automatic day clamping. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `setMonth` method updates the Bikram Sambat month for the current `NepaliDate` instance using a zero based month index from 0 for Baisakh to 11 for Chaitra. If the current day exceeds the total days in the destination month, the day is automatically clamped to the final valid day of that month.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
setMonth(month: number): void;
```

---

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- |
| `month` | `number` | Yes | **0-indexed** month integer (`0` for Baisakh to `11` for Chaitra). |

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `void`
* Mutates the current `NepaliDate` instance in place.

---

## Exceptions

| Error Message | Trigger Condition |
| :--- | :--- |
| `Invalid nepali month must be between 1 - 12` | Thrown if `month` is outside `0` to `11`. |

---

## Example

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// 2081 Baisakh 15 (month index 0)
const date = new NepaliDate("2081-01-15");

// Shift to Shrawan (month index 3)
date.setMonth(3);
console.log(date.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2081-04-15"
```

---

* [`date.getMonth()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/get-month): Retrieve the current month index.
* [`date.setDate()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/set-date): Mutate the day component.

## Page: date.startOfDay() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/start-of-day)
Description: [NodeJS] Return a new NepaliDate instance set to the first moment of the current day at midnight. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `startOfDay` method returns a new `NepaliDate` instance with time coordinates set to midnight at 00 hours, 00 minutes, 00 seconds, and 000 milliseconds. This is useful for date normalization and time neutral comparisons.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
startOfDay(): NepaliDate;
```

---

## Parameters

This method does not take any parameters.

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `NepaliDate`
* Returns a new cloned `NepaliDate` instance set to `00:00:00.000` on the same calendar day. The original instance is not modified.

---

## Examples

### Normalizing Date to Midnight

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date = new NepaliDate();
const start = date.startOfDay();

console.log(start.getHours()); // 0
console.log(start.getMinutes()); // 0
console.log(start.getSeconds()); // 0
console.log(start.getMilliseconds()); // 0
```

### Date Range Queries

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// Generate midnight boundaries for database filters
const fromDate = new NepaliDate("2081-02-10").startOfDay();
const toDate = new NepaliDate("2081-02-10").endOfDay();

console.log(fromDate.getEnglishDate().toISOString());
console.log(toDate.getEnglishDate().toISOString());
```

## Page: date.startOfMonth() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/start-of-month)
Description: [NodeJS] Return a new NepaliDate instance set to the first day of the current Bikram Sambat month. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `startOfMonth` method returns a new `NepaliDate` instance positioned on day 1 of the active Bikram Sambat month with time set to midnight. It is commonly used for monthly calendar views, statements, and aggregation buckets.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
startOfMonth(): NepaliDate;
```

---

## Parameters

This method does not take any parameters.

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `NepaliDate`
* Returns a new `NepaliDate` set to day `1` of the current year and month. The original instance is not modified.

---

## Examples

### Getting the First Day of the Month

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// 2081 Baisakh 25
const date = new NepaliDate(2081, 0, 25);

const start = date.startOfMonth();
console.log(start.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2081-01-01"
console.log(start.getDate()); // 1
```

### Calendar Header Computation

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const today = new NepaliDate();
const firstDay = today.startOfMonth();

// Find weekday that the month begins on
console.log(firstDay.getDay()); // 0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday, etc.
```

## Page: date.startOfWeek() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/start-of-week)
Description: [NodeJS] Return a new NepaliDate instance set to the first day of the week on Sunday. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `startOfWeek` method returns a new `NepaliDate` instance set to Sunday, the first day of the weekly cycle containing the current date. It serves as an anchor date for week based scheduling and calendar grids.

## Import

---

## Signature

## Parameters

## Return Value

* Returns a new `NepaliDate` instance set to the start of the week at midnight. The original instance is not modified.

---

## Exceptions

Throws an `Error` if `startOfWeek` is not an integer between `0` and `6`:

```typescript
"startOfWeek must be an integer between 0 and 6"
```

---

## Examples

### Default Week Start (Sunday)

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// Suppose date falls on a Wednesday (day 3)
const date = new NepaliDate("2081-02-16");

const weekStart = date.startOfWeek();
console.log(weekStart.getDay()); // 0 (Sunday)
console.log(weekStart.getHours()); // 0
console.log(weekStart.format("YYYY-MM-DD"));
```

### Custom Week Start (Monday)

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date = new NepaliDate("2081-02-16");

// Week starts on Monday (1)
const mondayStart = date.startOfWeek(1);
console.log(mondayStart.getDay()); // 1 (Monday)
```

---

## Related

* [`date.endOfWeek()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/end-of-week): Return the end of the week.
* [`date.startOfDay()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/start-of-day): Return the start of the day.
* [`date.getDay()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/get-day): Get current day of week index (`0-6`).

## Page: date.startOfYear() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/start-of-year)
Description: [NodeJS] Return a new NepaliDate instance set to the first day of the Bikram Sambat year on 1 Baisakh. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `startOfYear` method returns a new `NepaliDate` instance set to 1 Baisakh, the first day of the Bikram Sambat calendar year. This is useful for year to date financial tracking and annual summary reports.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
startOfYear(): NepaliDate;
```

---

## Parameters

This method does not take any parameters.

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `NepaliDate`
* Returns a new `NepaliDate` set to 1st Baisakh of the current year. The original instance is not modified.

---

## Examples

### Navigating to Bikram Sambat New Year

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// Any date within 2081 BS
const date = new NepaliDate("2081-08-15");

const newYear = date.startOfYear();
console.log(newYear.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2081-01-01"
console.log(newYear.getMonth()); // 0 (Baisakh)
console.log(newYear.getDate()); // 1
```

### Year-to-Date Calculations

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const today = new NepaliDate("2081-06-15");
const yearStart = today.startOfYear();

const daysElapsed = today.diff(yearStart, "day");
console.log(daysElapsed); // Number of days since start of the year
```

## Page: date.toString() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/methods/to-string)
Description: [NodeJS] Return the default string representation of a NepaliDate instance in standard year, month, and day format. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `toString` method converts the `NepaliDate` instance into a standard readable date string formatted as year, month, and day separated by forward slashes. It provides a simple default serialization format suitable for logs and quick display.

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

## Signature

```typescript
toString(): string;
```

## Parameters

### Default Serialization

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// 2081 Baisakh 15 (month index 0)
const date = new NepaliDate(2081, 0, 15);

```

### String Interpolation

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

## Page: Quick Start (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/quick-start)
Description: [NodeJS] Practical guide and essential code examples to start working with Bikram Sambat dates in Node.js and TypeScript. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

This quick start guide demonstrates common practical workflows for creating dates, performing calendar arithmetic, formatting output strings, and converting between Gregorian and Bikram Sambat calendars. Use these examples as reference patterns for building date pickers, booking systems, financial tools, and general calendar features.

---

## 1. Creating and Inspecting Dates

Initialize dates representing the current moment, specific Bikram Sambat coordinates, or existing Gregorian dates:

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// Current date and time in Nepal
const now = new NepaliDate();

// Specific Bikram Sambat date (Year, 0-indexed Month, Day)
// Month 6 represents Kartik (0 = Baisakh, 6 = Kartik)
const constitutionDay = new NepaliDate(2072, 5, 3);

// Parse from standard string formats (YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY/MM/DD, YYYY.MM.DD)
const festivalDate = new NepaliDate("2081-07-15");

console.log(festivalDate.getYear()); // 2081
console.log(festivalDate.getMonth()); // 6 (0-indexed)
console.log(festivalDate.getDate()); // 15
console.log(festivalDate.getDay()); // 5 (0 = Sunday, 5 = Friday)
```

---

## 2. Converting Between AD and BS

For database persistence and external API integration, convert between Gregorian (AD) and Bikram Sambat (BS):

### Using Standalone Converter Functions

```typescript
import { ADtoBS, BStoAD } from "nepali-date-library";

// Convert Gregorian date string to Bikram Sambat
const bsDate = ADtoBS("2024-10-31");
console.log(bsDate); // "2081-07-15"

// Convert Bikram Sambat date string to Gregorian
const adDate = BStoAD("2081-07-15");
console.log(adDate); // "2024-10-31"
```

### Using the `NepaliDate` Class

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// From native JS Date to BS
const jsDate = new Date("2024-10-31T00:00:00.000Z");
const nepaliDate = new NepaliDate(jsDate);
console.log(nepaliDate.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2081-07-15"

// From BS instance to native JS Date
const nativeDate = nepaliDate.getEnglishDate();
console.log(nativeDate.toISOString()); // "2024-10-31T00:00:00.000Z"
```

---

## 3. Formatting Dates

Format dates with customizable masks and localized Devanagari script:

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date = new NepaliDate(2081, 6, 15);

// Standard English formatting
console.log(date.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2081-07-15"
console.log(date.format("DD MMMM YYYY")); // "15 Kartik 2081"
console.log(date.format("dddd, MMMM DD, YYYY")); // "Friday, Kartik 15, 2081"

// Devanagari script and numeral formatting
console.log(date.format("yyyy-mm-dd")); // "२०८१-०७-१५"
console.log(date.format("dd mmmm yyyy")); // "१५ कार्तिक २०८१"
```

---

## 4. Date Arithmetic

Manipulate dates while safely respecting variable month lengths:

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const date = new NepaliDate("2081-01-20");

// Adding and subtracting days
date.addDays(15);
console.log(date.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2081-02-04"

// Adding months
date.addMonths(2);
console.log(date.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2081-04-04"

// Month boundaries
const endOfMonth = date.clone().endOfMonth();
console.log(endOfMonth.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2081-04-32"
```

---

## 5. Nepalese Fiscal Year Handling

Automate Nepal's Shrawan-to-Ashadh fiscal calendar calculations:

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// Current active fiscal year integer
const currentFY = NepaliDate.getCurrentFiscalYear();
console.log(currentFY); // 2081

// Get all 4 fiscal quarters for the current cycle
const quarters = NepaliDate.getFiscalYearQuarters(currentFY);
console.log(quarters.Q1.start.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2081-04-01"
console.log(quarters.Q1.end.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2081-06-30"
```

---

## Page: NepaliDate.getCalendarDays() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/static/get-calendar-days)
Description: [NodeJS] Static utility to generate a complete forty two cell calendar grid matrix for any month and year. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `getCalendarDays` static method generates a complete forty two cell grid structure representing six rows of seven days for displaying a monthly calendar view. It includes trailing days from the previous month and leading days from the next month to fill out the matrix, simplifying the creation of date pickers and visual calendar components.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
static getCalendarDays(
  year: number,
  month: number
): {
  prevRemainingDays: number;
  prevMonth: { year: number; month: number; days: number[] };
  currentMonth: { year: number; month: number; days: number[] };
  nextMonth: { year: number; month: number; days: number[] };
  remainingDays: number;
};
```

---

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- |
| `year` | `number` | Yes | Bikram Sambat year (e.g. `2081`). |
| `month` | `number` | Yes | Zero-indexed month (`0-11`, where `0` is Baisakh and `11` is Chaitra). |

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `Object` containing calendar grid sections:
  * `prevRemainingDays`: Number of leading days from the previous month needed to reach the first day's weekday.
  * `prevMonth`: Object containing `year`, `month`, and `days` array for preceding filler dates.
  * `currentMonth`: Object containing `year`, `month`, and `days` array (`1` through `daysInMonth`) for the active month.
  * `nextMonth`: Object containing `year`, `month`, and `days` array for succeeding filler dates to complete 42 cells.
  * `remainingDays`: Number of trailing days in `nextMonth`.

---

## Exceptions

Throws an `Error` if the year or month index is invalid:

```typescript
"Invalid year or month"
```

---

## Examples

### Building a Monthly UI Calendar Grid

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// Generate grid for Baisakh 2081
const grid = NepaliDate.getCalendarDays(2081, 0);

console.log("Leading days count:", grid.prevRemainingDays);
console.log("Leading days:", grid.prevMonth.days);
console.log("Active month days:", grid.currentMonth.days);
console.log("Trailing days:", grid.nextMonth.days);
```

### Rendering a 42-Cell React Calendar

```tsx
import React from "react";
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

export function NepaliCalendarView({ year, month }: { year: number; month: number }) {
  const grid = NepaliDate.getCalendarDays(year, month);

  return (
    <div className="grid grid-cols-7 gap-1">
      {/* Leading days from previous month */}
      {grid.prevMonth.days.map((d) => (
        <div key={`prev-${d}`} className="text-gray-400 p-2 text-center">
          {d}
        </div>
      ))}

      {/* Active month days */}
      {grid.currentMonth.days.map((d) => (
        <div key={`curr-${d}`} className="font-semibold p-2 text-center">
          {d}
        </div>
      ))}

      {/* Trailing days from next month */}
      {grid.nextMonth.days.map((d) => (
        <div key={`next-${d}`} className="text-gray-400 p-2 text-center">
          {d}
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

---

## Related

* [`date.daysInMonth()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/days-in-month): Total number of days in the month.
* [`date.getWeeksInMonth()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/get-weeks-in-month): Number of week rows needed.
* [`NepaliDate.isValid()`](/docs/nodejs/static/is-valid): Date validation.

## Page: NepaliDate.getDayName() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/static/get-day-name)
Description: [NodeJS] Static utility to retrieve the localized English or Nepali name for any day of the week index. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `getDayName` static method converts a numeric weekday index from 0 for Sunday through 6 for Saturday into its localized name. It supports both English and Nepali Devanagari script output, allowing flexible localization across international and local application interfaces.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
static getDayName(day: number, short?: boolean, nepali?: boolean): string;
```

---

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| `day` | `number` | Yes | - | Day of week index (`0-6`, where `0` is Sunday and `6` is Saturday). |
| `short` | `boolean` | No | `false` | When `true`, returns the abbreviated 3-letter or short weekday name. |
| `nepali` | `boolean` | No | `false` | When `true`, returns the weekday name in Devanagari script. |

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `string`
* Localized day of week name string.

---

## Exceptions

Throws an `Error` if `day` is less than `0` or greater than `6`:

```typescript
"Invalid day index, must be between 0-6"
```

---

## Output Reference Matrix

| Day Index | Default (`short: false, nepali: false`) | Short English (`short: true, nepali: false`) | Nepali Full (`short: false, nepali: true`) | Nepali Short (`short: true, nepali: true`) |
| :---: | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `0` | `"Sunday"` | `"Sun"` | `"आइतबार"` | `"आइत"` |
| `1` | `"Monday"` | `"Mon"` | `"सोमबार"` | `"सोम"` |
| `2` | `"Tuesday"` | `"Tue"` | `"मंगलबार"` | `"मंगल"` |
| `3` | `"Wednesday"` | `"Wed"` | `"बुधबार"` | `"बुध"` |
| `4` | `"Thursday"` | `"Thu"` | `"बिहिबार"` | `"बिहि"` |
| `5` | `"Friday"` | `"Fri"` | `"शुक्रबार"` | `"शुक्र"` |
| `6` | `"Saturday"` | `"Sat"` | `"शनिबार"` | `"शनि"` |

---

## Examples

### Generating Weekday Labels for UI

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// Default English
console.log(NepaliDate.getDayName(0)); // "Sunday"

// English Short
console.log(NepaliDate.getDayName(0, true)); // "Sun"

// Nepali Devanagari Full
console.log(NepaliDate.getDayName(0, false, true)); // "आइतबार"

// Nepali Devanagari Short
console.log(NepaliDate.getDayName(0, true, true)); // "आइत"
```

## Page: NepaliDate.isValid() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/static/is-valid)
Description: [NodeJS] Static validation function to verify whether a given year, month, and day combination forms a valid Bikram Sambat date. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The static `isValid` method verifies whether a specified Bikram Sambat year, month index, and day number represent a real calendar date. It consults verified historical data tables to confirm that the year falls within the supported range of 1976 through 2100 BS and that the day number does not exceed the actual number of days in that specific month.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
static isValid(year: number, month: number, day: number): boolean;
```

---

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- |
| `year` | `number` | Yes | Bikram Sambat year (e.g. `2081`). Supported range: `1976` to `2100`. |
| `month` | `number` | Yes | Zero-indexed month (`0-11`, where `0` is Baisakh and `11` is Chaitra). |
| `day` | `number` | Yes | Day of the month (`1-32`). |

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `boolean`
* Returns `true` if the year is within supported range, month is between `0` and `11`, and day does not exceed the exact number of days in that month; otherwise returns `false`.

---

## Examples

### Pre-validating User Input

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

// 2081 Baisakh 31 is valid (Baisakh has 31 days)
console.log(NepaliDate.isValid(2081, 0, 31)); // true

// 2081 Baisakh 32 does not exist
console.log(NepaliDate.isValid(2081, 0, 32)); // false

// Month index must be 0-11
console.log(NepaliDate.isValid(2081, 12, 1)); // false
```

### Form Input Validation Guard

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

function createNepaliEvent(y: number, m: number, d: number) {
  if (!NepaliDate.isValid(y, m, d)) {
    throw new Error(`Invalid Bikram Sambat date: ${y}-${m + 1}-${d}`);
  }
  return new NepaliDate(y, m, d);
}
```

* [`date.daysInMonth()`](/docs/nodejs/methods/days-in-month): Query total days in a month.

## Page: NepaliDate.maximum() (NodeJS) (/docs/nodejs/static/maximum)
Description: [NodeJS] Static method returning the maximum supported date boundary for the NepaliDate calendar engine. Official API reference and code examples for NodeJS / TypeScript.

The `maximum` static method returns a native JavaScript Date object representing the latest Gregorian date supported by the library calendar engine. This corresponds to the final day of Chaitra in year 2100 BS and serves as an upper bound for date validation and calendar limits.

---

## Import

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
static maximum(): Date;
```

---

## Parameters

This method does not take any parameters.

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `Date`
* Returns a standard JavaScript `Date` instance representing the absolute upper limit of the calendar mapping dataset.

---

## Examples

### Checking Upper Calendar Limit

```typescript
import { NepaliDate } from "nepali-date-library";

const maxDate = NepaliDate.maximum();
console.log(maxDate.toISOString());

// Converting maximum back to NepaliDate
const nepaliMax = new NepaliDate(maxDate);
console.log(nepaliMax.format("YYYY-MM-DD")); // "2100-12-30" (or 31)
```

## Page: What is Nepali Date? (Origination & Calendar) (/docs/origination)
Description: Deep dive into the origins, history, astronomical foundation, calendar mechanics, and timeline of Bikram Sambat (विक्रम संवत्).

The **Nepali Date** is based on the **Bikram Sambat** (Devanagari: **विक्रम संवत्**, abbreviated as **BS** or **B.S.**), the official national civil calendar of **Nepal**. 

Used across all organs of the Nepalese state—from parliamentary legislation and Supreme Court decrees to banking operations, taxation, school academic sessions, and day-to-day citizen records—Bikram Sambat is a sophisticated **solar sidereal calendar** with roots extending over two millennia.

---

## Historical Genesis of Bikram Sambat

### The Founding in 57 BCE
Bikram Sambat originated in **57 BCE (Before Common Era)** in the ancient city of **Ujjain** (in modern Madhya Pradesh, India). According to widespread historical tradition, the era was instituted by **King Vikramaditya of Ujjain** to commemorate his decisive military victory over the invading Saka (Indo-Scythian) forces, liberating the region and relieving the financial debt of his citizens.

Because the era was inaugurated in 57 BCE, Bikram Sambat is approximately **56.7 years ahead** of the Western Gregorian calendar (Common Era / AD).

### Evolution of the Era's Inscriptional Name
Epigraphic and numismatic records show that the name of this calendar era evolved across three distinct phases:

1. **Krita Era (कृत संवत्)**: Earliest stone inscriptions from the 3rd to 5th centuries CE referred to this system as *Krita*, possibly honoring a foundational event or sovereign leader.
2. **Malava Era (मालव संवत्)**: Between the 5th and 9th centuries CE, the era was called *Malava Gana Sambat* (the era of the Malava republic), corresponding to the migration and governance of the Malava tribe.
3. **Vikrama Samvat (विक्रम संवत्)**: By the 9th and 10th centuries CE, starting prominently around the Dholpur stone inscription (dated 842 CE / 898 BS), the era became permanently identified with King Vikramaditya.

---

## The Calendar Eras of Nepal

Nepal has one of the world's richest epigraphic and calendar traditions, having utilized several prominent eras throughout its documented history:

### 1. Saka Sambat (शक संवत् - 78 CE)
Introduced in ancient Nepal during the Licchavi period, the Saka Sambat was the primary calendar of early royal inscriptions. The oldest dated stone epigraph in Nepal—the pillar inscription of **King Manadeva I at the Changu Narayan Temple**—is dated **386 Saka Sambat (464 CE / 521 BS)**.

### 2. Manadeva Sambat / Amshuverma Era (576 CE)
During the late Licchavi period under rulers such as King Amshuverma and King Jisnugupta, a shortened regional calendar system known as the Manadeva Sambat was employed across the Kathmandu Valley for public administration and religious foundations.

### 3. Nepal Sambat (नेपाल संवत् - 879 CE / 936 BS)
Founded by **Shankhadhar Sakhwa** on Kartik Shukla Pratipada in 879 CE after he cleared the debts of all citizens in the Kathmandu Valley during the reign of King Raghavadeva. Nepal Sambat served as the principal civic, lunar, and commercial calendar of the Malla Dynasty (1200–1768 CE) and remains revered today as a national heritage calendar of Nepal.

### 4. Bikram Sambat in Ancient and Medieval Nepal
While Nepal Sambat predominated in the Kathmandu Valley's domestic trade, Bikram Sambat maintained continuous usage across western and northern Nepal:
- In the **Khasa Malla Empire** of the Karnali basin (centered in the Sinja Valley, Jumla), Bikram Sambat was the undisputed official calendar. The **Dullu Stone Pillar of King Prithvi Malla** (located in Dailekh) is engraved in Bikram Sambat **1414 BS (1357 CE)** using the ancient Khas language.
- King Jayasthiti Malla (reigned 1382–1395 CE) and King Pratap Malla of Kathmandu utilized Bikram Sambat alongside Nepal Sambat in stone treaties, temple edicts, and Sanskrit panegyrics.

### 5. Unification and Official Adoption in Nepal (1768–1901 CE)
When **King Prithvi Narayan Shah of Gorkha** unified Nepal and established Kathmandu as the capital in **1825 BS (1768 CE)**, he adopted Bikram Sambat as the standard calendar for royal seals (*Lal Mohar*), military directives, treaties, and administrative governance.

In **1958 BS (1901 CE)**, during the premiership of Rana Prime Minister **Chandra Shumsher Jung Bahadur Rana**, Bikram Sambat was formally promulgated by imperial decree as the **sole official civil and administrative calendar of the Kingdom of Nepal**, standardizing astronomical solar calculations across all government offices.

---

## Astronomical Foundations & Calendar Mechanics

Unlike the Western Gregorian calendar, which is a **solar tropical** calendar based on the cycle of the seasons (equinoxes and solstices), Bikram Sambat is a **solar sidereal (*Nirayana*)** calendar governed by the principles of classical Hindu astronomy (*Surya Siddhanta*).

### 1. The Sidereal Solar Year (*Nirayana Saur Varsha*)
A sidereal year is the time it takes the Earth to complete one full revolution around the Sun relative to the fixed stars.
- The tropical year (used by Gregorian) equals approximately **365.2422 days**.
- The sidereal year (used by Bikram Sambat) equals approximately **365.25636 days**.
- Due to the precession of the equinoxes (*Ayanamsha*), the sidereal year advances forward relative to the tropical year by approximately **1 day every 71.6 years**.

### 2. Solar Ingress (*Sankranti*)
In Bikram Sambat, the first day of every month begins upon the Sun's transit (*Sankranti*) from one zodiac constellation (*Rashi*) into the next:

- **Mesha Sankranti (Aries Ingress)**: Marks the entrance of the Sun into the constellation of Mesha (Aries). This exact astronomical occurrence defines **Baisakh 1**, celebrating **Nepali New Year (*Nawa Barsha*)**.
- **Makar Sankranti (Capricorn Ingress)**: Marks the Sun's entrance into Makara, signaling the winter solstice turning point and the festival of **Maghe Sankranti**.

### 3. Kepler's Second Law & Variable Month Lengths (29 to 32 Days)
A defining characteristic of Bikram Sambat is that **month lengths vary between 29 and 32 days from year to year**.

This is not arbitrary; it is a direct consequence of celestial mechanics:
1. According to **Kepler's Second Law**, Earth travels faster along its elliptical orbit when it is closest to the Sun (perihelion, occurring in early January) and slower when it is farthest from the Sun (aphelion, occurring in early July).
2. Because the Earth moves faster during the northern hemisphere's winter, the Sun appears to traverse the winter constellations (Dhanu, Makara, Kumbha) in less time. Consequently, winter months like **Kartik, Mangsir, Poush, and Magh** typically span **29 to 30 days**.
3. During the northern hemisphere's summer, the Earth moves slower in its orbit, taking longer to traverse constellations like Mithuna and Karkata. Consequently, summer months like **Jestha, Ashadh, Shrawan, and Bhadra** typically span **31 to 32 days**.

> [!NOTE]
> Because the exact moment of Sankranti can occur at any hour of the day or night, canonical Panchanga rules determine whether the new month begins on the same solar day (if Sankranti occurs before sunset or noon) or the following solar day. This produces variations where a given month may have 31 days in one year, but 32 days in another.

---

## The 12 Nepali Months & Seasonal Cycles (*Ritus*)

The Bikram Sambat year consists of **12 solar months** categorized into **six traditional two-month seasons (*Ritus*)**:

| # | Month (English) | Month (नेपाली) | Zodiac Sign (*Rashi*) | Season (*Ritu*) | Gregorian Span | Days Range |
| :---: | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :---: |
| **1** | **Baisakh** | बैशाख | Mesha (मेष - Aries) | Basanta (वसन्तः - Spring) | Apr 13/14 – May 13/14 | 30 – 31 |
| **2** | **Jestha** | जेठ | Vrishabha (वृषभ - Taurus) | Grishma (ग्रीष्म - Summer) | May 14/15 – Jun 14/15 | 31 – 32 |
| **3** | **Ashadh** | असार | Mithuna (मिथुन - Gemini) | Grishma (ग्रीष्म - Summer) | Jun 15/16 – Jul 15/16 | 31 – 32 |
| **4** | **Shrawan** | श्रावण / साउन | Karkata (कर्कट - Cancer) | Barsha (वर्षा - Monsoon) | Jul 16/17 – Aug 16/17 | 31 – 32 |
| **5** | **Bhadra** | भाद्र / भदौ | Simha (सिंह - Leo) | Barsha (वर्षा - Monsoon) | Aug 17/18 – Sep 16/17 | 31 – 32 |
| **6** | **Ashwin** | आश्विन / असोज | Kanya (कन्या - Virgo) | Sharad (शरद् - Autumn) | Sep 17/18 – Oct 17/18 | 30 – 31 |
| **7** | **Kartik** | कार्तिक / कात्तिक | Tula (तुला - Libra) | Sharad (शरद् - Autumn) | Oct 18/19 – Nov 15/16 | 29 – 30 |
| **8** | **Mangsir** | मार्ग / मंसिर | Vrischika (वृश्चिक - Scorpio) | Hemanta (हेमन्त - Late Autumn) | Nov 16/17 – Dec 15/16 | 29 – 30 |
| **9** | **Poush** | पौष / पुस | Dhanu (धनु - Sagittarius) | Hemanta (हेमन्त - Late Autumn) | Dec 16/17 – Jan 14/15 | 29 – 30 |
| **10** | **Magh** | माघ | Makara (मकर - Capricorn) | Shishir (शिशिर - Winter) | Jan 15/16 – Feb 12/13 | 29 – 30 |
| **11** | **Falgun** | फाल्गुन / फागुन | Kumbha (कुम्भ - Aquarius) | Shishir (शिशिर - Winter) | Feb 13/14 – Mar 13/14 | 29 – 30 |
| **12** | **Chaitra** | चैत्र / चैत | Mina (मीन - Pisces) | Basanta (वसन्तः - Spring) | Mar 14/15 – Apr 12/13 | 30 – 31 |

---

## Days of the Week (*Vaar*)

The seven-day week in Bikram Sambat mirrors the classical planetary order (*Navagraha*):

| Day (English) | Day (नेपाली) | Devanagari | Planetary Body | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Sunday** | Aaitabar | आइतबार | Aditya / Surya (सूर्य) | Day of the Sun |
| **Monday** | Sombar | सोमबार | Soma / Chandra (चन्द्र) | Day of the Moon |
| **Tuesday** | Mangalbar | मङ्गलबार | Mangala (मङ्गल) | Day of Mars |
| **Wednesday** | Budhabar | बुधबार | Budha (बुध) | Day of Mercury |
| **Thursday** | Bihibar | बिहिबार | Brihaspati / Guru (बृहस्पति) | Day of Jupiter |
| **Friday** | Shukrabar | शुक्रबार | Shukra (शुक्र) | Day of Venus |
| **Saturday** | Sanibar | शनिबार | Shani (शनि) | Day of Saturn |

---

## The Nepalese Fiscal Year (*Aarthik Barsha*)

In Nepal, both public finance and commercial corporate reporting run on an official fiscal cycle defined entirely by Bikram Sambat dates:

- **Fiscal Year Start**: **1 Shrawan** (approximately mid-July).
- **Fiscal Year End**: **Last day of Ashadh** (approximately mid-July of the following year).
- **Format**: Written as `YYYY/YY` in BS (for example, `2081/82 BS`).
- **Quarterly Accounting Windows**:
  - **Q1 (First Quarter)**: Shrawan 1 – Kartik end
  - **Q2 (Second Quarter)**: Mangsir 1 – Poush end
  - **Q3 (Third Quarter)**: Magh 1 – Chaitra end
  - **Q4 (Fourth Quarter)**: Baisakh 1 – Ashadh end

All corporate income tax filings, government budget announcements (constitutionally mandated on 15 Jestha BS), and audited balance sheets operate strictly within this fiscal boundary.

---

## Bikram Sambat (BS) vs. Gregorian (AD) Comparison

| Dimension | Bikram Sambat (BS) | Gregorian Calendar (AD / CE) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **System Classification** | Solar Sidereal (*Nirayana*) | Solar Tropical (*Sayana*) |
| **Reference Epoch** | 57 BCE (Victory of Vikramaditya) | 1 CE (Traditional Anno Domini) |
| **Year Discrepancy** | Approx **56 years, 8 months ahead** | Baseline (+0) |
| **New Year Day** | **1 Baisakh** (mid-April) | January 1 |
| **Month Calculation** | Astrological solar ingress (*Sankranti*) | Arbitrarily fixed human convention |
| **Month Lengths** | Variable dynamically: **29, 30, 31, 32 days** | Fixed: 28/29, 30, 31 days |
| **Leap Day Mechanism** | Natural solar variance across constellations | Quadrennial Leap Day (+1 day in Feb) |
| **Certifying Body** | **Nepal Panchanga Nirnayak Samiti** | International Earth Rotation Service (IERS) |
| **Official Civil Status** | **National Calendar of Nepal** | International standard (ISO 8601) |

---

## Technical Implications for Software Engineering

Building software applications that handle Bikram Sambat presents unique architectural requirements that do not exist with purely algorithmic calendars:

### 1. Mathematical Algorithms Cannot Predict Month Lengths
In the Gregorian calendar, determining if a year is a leap year requires a simple formula:
```
(year % 4 === 0 && year % 100 !== 0) || (year % 400 === 0)
```
In Bikram Sambat, **no such modular formula exists**. Because month lengths depend on the precise astronomical minute of the Sun's transit across constellations as observed from Kathmandu, month lengths are certified yearly by the **Nepal Panchanga Nirnayak Samiti**.

### 2. Comprehensive Calendar Mapping & Annual Ashwin Verification
Because modular formulas cannot predict month lengths, reliable date libraries must embed pre-computed lookup matrices containing verified month lengths for historical and modern Bikram Sambat years.

The **Nepali Date Library** embeds calendar mapping data spanning **1976 BS through 2100 BS** (more than 124 years). Because the official Government of Nepal calendar for the upcoming year is released annually in the month of **Ashwin (Ashoj)** by the **Nepal Panchanga Nirnayak Samiti**, the library verifies dates up to the current active year and incorporates authoritative government updates annually upon publication.

### 3. Database Architecture Recommendation
When architecting systems supporting Bikram Sambat:
- **Storage Layer**: Store all temporal values in databases as standard UTC timestamps or ISO-8601 Gregorian dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`).
- **Application Layer**: Use `nepali-date-library` to convert UTC timestamps to Bikram Sambat dates for UI display, fiscal reports, date pickers, and localized formatting.
- **Form Inputs**: Convert user-entered Bikram Sambat values to Gregorian prior to saving in persistent storage.

### 4. Nepal Standard Time (NPT)
Nepal Standard Time is **UTC+05:45**, one of the few non-hourly timezones in the world. It is calculated based on the meridian passing through the summit of **Mount Gauri Shankar** at longitude **86°15' East**. When performing date calculations near midnight, ensure that your application accounts for the +05:45 offset to avoid single-day boundary shifts.

## Page: Project Overview (/docs/overview)
Description: Comprehensive overview of the Nepali Date Library multi-language ecosystem, live package metrics, architecture, and developer profile.

The **Nepali Date Library** is an open-source, production-grade computational suite engineered to bring accurate, standardized, and zero-dependency **Bikram Sambat (BS)** date operations to modern software ecosystems across **Node.js / TypeScript**, **Python**, and **PHP**.

Whether you are building financial banking software adhering to Nepal's Shrawan-to-Ashadh fiscal calendar, government enterprise portals, e-commerce checkouts, or mobile applications, the suite provides unified semantics and continuously audited calendar tables.

---

## Ecosystem Distributions & Metrics

The library is officially distributed across the primary package registries of each supported language ecosystem:

<EcosystemOverview />

---

## Core Architectural Pillars

The library suite is built around five foundational design principles:

### 1. Zero External Dependencies
Every package in the suite is built from the ground up without runtime external dependencies. This eliminates supply-chain risks, avoids version conflicts, and keeps bundle footprints minimal.

### 2. Standardized Cross-Language API
Developers working across full-stack applications (e.g., a Python backend with a Node.js frontend or a PHP Laravel service with a TypeScript worker) enjoy identical method names, formatting tokens, and date manipulation semantics.

### 3. Annual Calendar Verification & 124-Year Range (1976 – 2100 BS)
Because Bikram Sambat months are based on solar ingress (*Sankranti*) and vary from 29 to 32 days based on astronomical solar transit, official month lengths are determined each year by the **Nepal Panchanga Nirnayak Samiti** (नेपाल पञ्चाङ्ग निर्णायक समिति). Every year around the month of **Ashwin (Ashoj)**, when the Government of Nepal officially gazettes the upcoming year's calendar, the library audits and updates its mapping data. Dates up to the current active calendar year are verified against official gazettes, while future projections up to 2100 BS are systematically updated each year upon official publication.

### 4. High-Throughput Performance
All date conversions and arithmetic execute in under a few microseconds, making the library suitable for high-frequency database batch migrations, real-time analytics pipelines, and edge compute functions.

### 5. Built-In Nepalese Fiscal Year Logic
Native support for Nepal's official fiscal calendar (*Aarthik Barsha*), running from 1 Shrawan to the final day of Ashadh, including quarter categorization (Q1 to Q4) and fiscal year string formatting (`2081/82`).

| **Zero Runtime Dependencies** | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| **Package Distribution** | npm / yarn / pnpm | PyPI (pip / uv / poetry) | Packagist (Composer) |

It handles bidirectional conversion between Bikram Sambat and Gregorian calendars, date arithmetic, custom string formatting, fiscal year calculations, and calendar grid generation for PHP web applications and enterprise systems.

## Installation

Install the package via Composer:

```bash
composer require sghimire/nepali-date-library
```

---

## Quick Example

```php
<?php

require 'vendor/autoload.php';

use NepaliDateLibrary\NepaliDate;
use function NepaliDateLibrary\ADtoBS;
use function NepaliDateLibrary\BStoAD;

// Current Nepali date
$today = new NepaliDate();
echo $today->format('YYYY-MM-DD');

// Specific Bikram Sambat date (month 0 is Baisakh)
$event = new NepaliDate(2081, 6, 15);
echo $event->format('dddd, MMMM DD, YYYY');

// Standalone date conversion helpers
$bsDate = ADtoBS('2024-11-15');
$adDate = BStoAD('2081-07-30');
```

| Feature | Support | Description |
| :--- | :---: | :--- |
| **Bikram Sambat Calendar Engine** | Yes | Calendar matrix spanning 1976 through 2100 BS, audited and updated annually each Ashwin. |
| **Bidirectional AD to BS Conversion** | Yes | Standalone conversion functions and full object instances. |
| **Date Arithmetic** | Yes | Add and subtract days, months, and years with automatic rollover. |
| **Fiscal Year Operations** | Yes | Official Nepalese fiscal calendar starting on 1 Shrawan. |
| **Custom Format Patterns** | Yes | Token formatting for year, month, weekday, and Devanagari script. |
| **Calendar Grid Builder** | Yes | Forty two cell matrix generation for calendar interfaces. |

---

## Package Information

| Specification | Details |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Composer Package** | [`sghimire/nepali-date-library`](https://packagist.org/packages/sghimire/nepali-date-library) |
| **Repository** | [GitHub](https://github.com/SandipGhimire/Nepali-Date-Library-PHP) |
| **Supported PHP** | PHP 7.1, 7.2, 7.3, 7.4, 8.0, 8.1, 8.2, 8.3, 8.4+ |
| **License** | MIT License |

## Page: new NepaliDate() (PHP) (/docs/php/class/constructor)
Description: [PHP] Constructor overloads and initialization options for creating NepaliDate instances in PHP. Official API reference and code examples for PHP.

The `NepaliDate` constructor creates instances representing specific points in time mapped to the Bikram Sambat calendar system. You can construct an instance representing the current moment, provide separate year, month, and day integers, supply a standard date string, or pass a native PHP DateTimeInterface object. Bikram Sambat months are indexed starting from 0 for Baisakh through 11 for Chaitra.

---

## Import

```php
use NepaliDateLibrary\NepaliDate;
```

---

## Signatures

```php
// 1. Current Date and Time
new NepaliDate(): NepaliDate;

// 2. From PHP DateTimeInterface object
new NepaliDate(DateTimeInterface $date): NepaliDate;

// 3. From another NepaliDate instance (copy constructor)
new NepaliDate(NepaliDate $date): NepaliDate;

// 4. From Bikram Sambat date string
new NepaliDate(string $dateString): NepaliDate;

// 5. From separate Year, Month, Day integers
new NepaliDate(int $year, int $month, int $day): NepaliDate;

// 6. From Unix millisecond timestamp
new NepaliDate(int $timestampMs): NepaliDate;
```

---

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- |
| `$yearOrDate` | `int`, `string`, `DateTimeInterface`, `NepaliDate`, `null` | No | Year integer, ISO date string, DateTimeInterface, or another NepaliDate instance. |
| `$month` | `int`, `null` | No | Zero based month index from `0` for Baisakh to `11` for Chaitra when specifying integers. |
| `$day` | `int`, `null` | No | Day of the month from `1` to `32` depending on the year and month. |

---

## Return Value

* **Type**: `NepaliDate`
* **Description**: A newly instantiated `NepaliDate` instance representing the specified point in time.

---

## Examples

### Current Date and Time

```php
use NepaliDateLibrary\NepaliDate;

$now = new NepaliDate();
echo $now->format('YYYY-MM-DD');
```

### From Numeric Coordinates

```php
// Month 0 is Baisakh, Day 1
$newYear = new NepaliDate(2081, 0, 1);
echo $newYear->format('YYYY-MM-DD'); // "2081-01-01"
```

### From Date String

```php
// Delimiters can be hyphens, slashes, or dots
$date1 = new NepaliDate('2081-07-15');
$date2 = new NepaliDate('2081/07/15');
$date3 = new NepaliDate('2081.07.15');
```

### From PHP DateTimeImmutable

```php
use DateTimeImmutable;
use DateTimeZone;
use NepaliDateLibrary\NepaliDate;

$adDate = DateTimeImmutable::createFromFormat('!Y-m-d', '2024-10-31', new DateTimeZone('UTC'));
$nd = new NepaliDate($adDate);
echo $nd->format('YYYY-MM-DD'); // "2081-07-15"
```

---

## Related

* [`Instance Properties`](/docs/php/class/properties): Getters for calendar coordinates.
* [`date->set()`](/docs/php/methods/set): Update year, month, and day coordinates simultaneously.

## Page: Instance Properties & Getters (PHP) (/docs/php/class/properties)
Description: [PHP] Guide to property encapsulation and public getters available on every NepaliDate instance in PHP. Official API reference and code examples for PHP.

In PHP the `NepaliDate` class follows strict object oriented encapsulation principles. Internal state properties are private to protect calendar integrity, while public getter methods provide access to the four digit Bikram Sambat year, zero based month index, day of the month, and underlying Gregorian timestamp.

---

## Public Getters Reference

| Method | Return Type | Description | Value Range |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `$date->getYear()` | `int` | The four digit Bikram Sambat year. | `1976` to `2100` |
| `$date->getMonth()` | `int` | The zero based Bikram Sambat month index. | `0` (Baisakh) to `11` (Chaitra) |
| `$date->getDate()` | `int` | The day of the month. | `1` to `32` |
| `$date->getEnglishDate()` | `DateTimeImmutable` | The equivalent Gregorian date in UTC. | Native PHP DateTimeImmutable |
| `$date->getTime()` | `int` | The Unix epoch millisecond timestamp. | 64-bit integer timestamp |

---

## Examples

### Reading Coordinates via Getters

```php
use NepaliDateLibrary\NepaliDate;

$date = new NepaliDate('2081-07-15');

echo $date->getYear();            // 2081
echo $date->getMonth();           // 6 (Kartik is index 6)
echo $date->getDate();            // 15
echo $date->getEnglishDate()->format('Y-m-d'); // "2024-10-31"
```

### Working with Month Indices

Because `$date->getMonth()` is zero based, add 1 when outputting conventional month numbers:

```php
$humanMonth = $date->getMonth() + 1; // 7
echo NepaliDate::getMonthName($date->getMonth()); // "Kartik"
```

---

## Related

* [`date->getYear()`](/docs/php/methods/get-year): Getter method for year.
* [`date->getMonth()`](/docs/php/methods/get-month): Getter method for month index.
* [`date->getDate()`](/docs/php/methods/get-date): Getter method for day of month.

## Page: Constants::$MONTH_EN (PHP) (/docs/php/constants/month-en)
Description: [PHP] Array containing standard romanized English names of all twelve Bikram Sambat calendar months. Official API reference and code examples for PHP.

The `Constants::$MONTH_EN` constant is an immutable array containing the official romanized English names of the twelve Bikram Sambat months. The array is indexed starting from 0 for Baisakh up to index 11 for Chaitra, making it convenient for looking up month names corresponding to numeric month values returned by date methods.

---

## Import

```php
use NepaliDateLibrary\Helper\Constants;
```

---

## Value

```php
Constants::$MONTH_EN = [
    "Baisakh",
    "Jestha",
    "Asar",
    "Shrawan",
    "Bhadra",
    "Aswin",
    "Kartik",
    "Mangsir",
    "Poush",
    "Magh",
    "Falgun",
    "Chaitra",
];
```

---

## Month Index Table

| Index | English Name | Approximate Gregorian Window |
| :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `0` | `"Baisakh"` | Mid April to Mid May |
| `1` | `"Jestha"` | Mid May to Mid June |
| `2` | `"Asar"` | Mid June to Mid July |
| `3` | `"Shrawan"` | Mid July to Mid August |
| `4` | `"Bhadra"` | Mid August to Mid September |
| `5` | `"Aswin"` | Mid September to Mid October |
| `6` | `"Kartik"` | Mid October to Mid November |
| `7` | `"Mangsir"` | Mid November to Mid December |
| `8` | `"Poush"` | Mid December to Mid January |
| `9` | `"Magh"` | Mid January to Mid February |
| `10` | `"Falgun"` | Mid February to Mid March |
| `11` | `"Chaitra"` | Mid March to Mid April |

---

## Example Usage

```php
use NepaliDateLibrary\NepaliDate;
use NepaliDateLibrary\Helper\Constants;

$date = new NepaliDate('2081-07-15');
$monthIndex = $date->getMonth();
echo Constants::$MONTH_EN[$monthIndex]; // "Kartik"
```

---

* [`Constants::$MONTH_NP`](/docs/php/constants/month-np): Full Devanagari Nepali month names.

## Page: Constants::$NEPALI_DATE_MAP (PHP) (/docs/php/constants/nepali-date-map)
Description: [PHP] Historical calendar mapping table storing verified day counts for every Bikram Sambat month between 1976 and 2100 BS. Official API reference and code examples for PHP.

The `Constants::$NEPALI_DATE_MAP` data structure contains the calendar matrix for the Bikram Sambat system spanning years 1976 through 2100 BS. Because Bikram Sambat months have variable day counts determined by astronomical solar calculations rather than fixed rules, this mapping table provides the definitive source of truth for conversions, day calculations, and month lengths.

> [!NOTE]
> Dates up to the active calendar year are verified against official publications from the **Nepal Panchanga Nirnayak Samiti** (नेपाल पञ्चाङ्ग निर्णायक समिति). Every year around the month of **Ashwin (Ashoj)**, when the official government calendar is gazetted for the subsequent year, this mapping table is audited and updated with exact solar ingress corrections.

---

## Import

```php
use NepaliDateLibrary\Helper\Constants;
```

---

## Structure

```php
class Constants
{
    /**
     * @var array<int, array{year:int, days:int[], totalDays:int, daysTillNow:int}>
     */
    public static $NEPALI_DATE_MAP;
}
```

---

## Field Reference

| Field | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `year` | `int` | The Bikram Sambat year integer between 1976 and 2100 BS. |
| `days` | `int[]` | Twelve integers specifying the exact day counts for each month from Baisakh to Chaitra. |
| `totalDays` | `int` | Total cumulative days in that specific calendar year. |
| `daysTillNow` | `int` | Cumulative day offset since the calendar epoch. |

---

## Example Usage

```php
use NepaliDateLibrary\Helper\Constants;

// Retrieve month day counts for year 2081 BS
$year2081 = null;
foreach (Constants::$NEPALI_DATE_MAP as $entry) {
    if ($entry['year'] === 2081) {
        $year2081 = $entry;
        break;
    }
}

echo "Days in Baisakh 2081: " . $year2081['days'][0]; // 31
```

---

* [`date->daysInMonth()`](/docs/php/methods/days-in-month): Query total days in a given month.
* [`NepaliDate::isValid()`](/docs/php/static/is-valid): Statically validate calendar coordinates.

## Page: Constants::$NUMBER_NP (PHP) (/docs/php/constants/number-np)
Description: [PHP] Array containing Devanagari numeral glyphs for digits zero through nine used for Nepali number localization. Official API reference and code examples for PHP.

The `Constants::$NUMBER_NP` constant is an array containing the ten Devanagari numeral characters representing digits 0 through 9 in Nepali script. It provides a direct lookup table for formatting numbers, years, dates, and currency values into native Devanagari script for Nepali language interfaces.

---

## Import

```php
use NepaliDateLibrary\Helper\Constants;
```

---

## Value

```php
Constants::$NUMBER_NP = ["०", "१", "२", "३", "४", "५", "६", "७", "८", "९"];
```

---

## Digit Lookup Table

| Index | Arabic Digit | Devanagari Numeral | Unicode Code Point |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| `0` | `0` | `०` | `U+0966` |
| `1` | `1` | `१` | `U+0967` |
| `2` | `2` | `२` | `U+0968` |
| `3` | `3` | `३` | `U+0969` |
| `4` | `4` | `४` | `U+096A` |
| `5` | `5` | `५` | `U+096B` |
| `6` | `6` | `६` | `U+096C` |
| `7` | `7` | `७` | `U+096D` |
| `8` | `8` | `८` | `U+096E` |
| `9` | `9` | `९` | `U+096F` |

---

## Examples

```php
use NepaliDateLibrary\Helper\Constants;

function toDevanagari(int $number): string
{
    $digits = str_split((string) $number);
    return implode('', array_map(function ($d) {
        return Constants::$NUMBER_NP[(int) $d];
    }, $digits));
}

echo toDevanagari(2081); // "२०८१"
```

```php
use NepaliDateLibrary\Helper\Constants;
```

---

## Value

```php
Constants::$WEEK_SHORT_NP = [
    "आ",
    "सो",
    "मं",
    "बु",
    "बि",
    "शु",
    "श",
];
```

---

## Weekday Abbreviation Table

| Index | Short Devanagari | Full Devanagari | English |
| :---: | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `0` | `आ` | आइतबार | Sunday |
| `1` | `सो` | सोमबार | Monday |
| `2` | `मं` | मंगलबार | Tuesday |
| `3` | `बु` | बुधबार | Wednesday |
| `4` | `बि` | बिहिबार | Thursday |
| `5` | `शु` | शुक्रबार | Friday |
| `6` | `श` | शनिबार | Saturday |

---

## Example Usage

```php
use NepaliDateLibrary\NepaliDate;
use NepaliDateLibrary\Helper\Constants;

$date = new NepaliDate('2081-07-15');
echo Constants::$WEEK_SHORT_NP[$date->getDay()]; // "शु"
```

---

## Related

* [`Constants::$WEEK_NP`](/docs/php/constants/week-np): Full Devanagari weekday names.
* [`Constants::$WEEK_SHORT_EN`](/docs/php/constants/week-short-en): Three letter English weekday abbreviations.
